# Overview



![Biomni Logo](https://github.com/snap-stanford/Biomni/blob/main/figs/biomni_logo.png?raw=true)

**Biomni** is a general-purpose biomedical AI agent that autonomously executes research tasks across diverse biomedical subfields. Developed at Stanford University and released under the Apache 2.0 license, it bridges the gap between large language model (LLM) reasoning and real-world biomedical computation by combining retrieval-augmented planning with code-based execution. Whether you're planning a CRISPR screen, annotating single-cell RNA-seq data, or predicting drug properties, Biomni translates natural language instructions into multi-step, tool-driven scientific workflows.

The current release is **v0.0.8** and is available both as a pip-installable package and as a no-code web interface at [biomni.stanford.edu](https://biomni.stanford.edu). This page introduces the project's high-level architecture, core capabilities, and how to navigate the rest of this documentation.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L1-L30), [biomni/version.py](biomni/version.py#L1-L2), [pyproject.toml](pyproject.toml#L1-L18)

## High-Level Architecture

At its core, Biomni follows a **reason → retrieve → execute** loop. A user submits a natural language query, the agent reasons about which tools and data are needed, retrieves the most relevant resources from its vast ecosystem, then generates and runs Python/R/bash code to produce results. This cycle repeats until the task is complete.

The following diagram shows how the major subsystems connect:

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph User["User Interface"]
        CLI["Python REPL"]
        GRADIO["Gradio Web UI"]
        WEB["biomni.stanford.edu"]
    end

    subgraph Agent["A1 Agent Core"]
        LLM["LLM Reasoning<br/>(Claude, GPT, Gemini, Biomni-R0, …)"]
        REACT["ReAct Reasoning Engine"]
        RETRIEVER["Tool Retriever"]
        REPL["Python/R/Bash REPL"]
    end

    subgraph Tools["Tool System"]
        REGISTRY["Tool Registry"]
        DOMAINS["20+ Domain Modules<br/>genomics · pharmacology · immunology …"]
        DB["Database Query Layer<br/>30+ biomedical APIs"]
        MCP["MCP Servers"]
    end

    subgraph Data["Data & Knowledge Layer"]
        LAKE["Data Lake<br/>(80+ curated datasets, ~11 GB)"]
        LIB["Software Libraries<br/>(Python · R · CLI tools)"]
        KNOW["Know-How Library<br/>(protocols · best practices)"]
    end

    CLI --> REACT
    GRADIO --> REACT
    WEB --> REACT

    REACT <--> LLM
    REACT --> RETRIEVER
    REACT --> REPL

    RETRIEVER --> REGISTRY
    RETRIEVER --> LAKE
    RETRIEVER --> LIB
    RETRIEVER --> KNOW

    REGISTRY --> DOMAINS
    REGISTRY --> DB
    REGISTRY --> MCP

    REPL --> DOMAINS
    REPL --> LAKE
    REPL --> LIB
```

The agent entry point is the **`A1`** class, which orchestrates everything from configuration loading to tool retrieval to code execution. On initialization, it downloads ~11 GB of curated data lake files from S3, builds a tool registry spanning 20+ domain modules, and sets up the LLM-backed reasoning pipeline. Users interact with `A1` through a single `agent.go("your task here")` call.

Sources: [biomni/agent/a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L46-L200), [biomni/agent/react.py](biomni/agent/react.py#L38-L54), [biomni/config.py](biomni/config.py#L1-L100)

## Core Capabilities

### Natural Language Task Execution

Biomni accepts free-form biomedical questions and autonomously breaks them into subtasks. It selects the right combination of tools, writes executable code, interprets results, and iterates until the task is resolved. The agent supports multiple LLM providers and can even run the specialized **Biomni-R0** reasoning model for biology-focused tasks.

| Capability | Description | Example Prompt |
|---|---|---|
| **CRISPR Design** | Plan screens, design sgRNAs, analyze editing outcomes | *"Plan a CRISPR screen to identify genes that regulate T cell exhaustion"* |
| **Single-Cell Analysis** | scRNA-seq annotation, embedding generation, cell type transfer | *"Perform scRNA-seq annotation at [PATH] and generate meaningful hypothesis"* |
| **Drug Discovery** | ADMET prediction, molecular docking, drug repurposing | *"Predict ADMET properties for this compound: CC(C)CC1=CC=C(C=C1)C(C)C(=O)O"* |
| **Literature Search** | PubMed, arXiv, Google Scholar queries | *"Find recent publications on CAR-T cell therapy for solid tumors"* |
| **Genomic Analysis** | Variant prioritization, GWAS analysis, ChIP-seq, Hi-C | *"Perform Bayesian fine-mapping on this GWAS summary statistics"* |
| **Database Queries** | 30+ biomedical APIs (UniProt, KEGG, ClinVar, cBioPortal, …) | *"Query UniProt for human TP53 protein domains"* |

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L60-L78), [biomni/tool/database.py](biomni/tool/database.py#L448-L4975)

### Extensive Biomedical Tool Ecosystem

Biomni provides over **20 domain-specific tool modules** covering the breadth of biomedical research. Each module contains dozens of Python functions decorated with metadata that the Tool Registry indexes for automatic discovery. The agent doesn't need to know which function to call — the retrieval system selects the right tools based on the task context.

| Domain Module | Key Functions | Lines of Code |
|---|---|---|
| **Genomics** | Cell type annotation, gene set enrichment, ChIP-seq, comparative genomics | ~2,760 |
| **Genetics** | CRISPR editing analysis, GWAS fine-mapping, PCR simulation, phylogeny | ~1,673 |
| **Pharmacology** | Drug docking, ADMET prediction, FDA queries, drug-drug interactions | ~4,283 |
| **Immunology** | Flow cytometry, immune cell tracking, cytokine analysis, IHC | ~1,973 |
| **Cell Biology** | Cell cycle analysis, FACS sorting, mitochondrial morphology | ~743 |
| **Molecular Biology** | Primer design, restriction digestion, Golden Gate assembly, plasmid annotation | ~2,223 |
| **Synthetic Biology** | Gene circuit simulation, codon optimization, metabolic modeling | ~1,352 |
| **Database Queries** | 30+ API integrations (UniProt, KEGG, ClinVar, cBioPortal, etc.) | ~4,975 |

> [!TIP]
> The tool count above reflects only the function definitions visible in the source modules. The actual executable surface area expands significantly because each tool can call downstream Python packages (over 70 libraries), R packages (DESeq2, Seurat, etc.), and CLI tools (samtools, bowtie2, bedtools, etc.) that are all pre-installed in the Biomni conda environment.

Sources: [biomni/tool/genomics.py](biomni/tool/genomics.py#L18-L2442), [biomni/tool/genetics.py](biomni/tool/genetics.py#L1-L1673), [biomni/tool/pharmacology.py](biomni/tool/pharmacology.py#L13-L4234), [biomni/tool/immunology.py](biomni/tool/immunology.py#L1-L1973), [biomni/tool/cell_biology.py](biomni/tool/cell_biology.py#L1-L743), [biomni/tool/molecular_biology.py](biomni/tool/molecular_biology.py#L15-L2223), [biomni/tool/synthetic_biology.py](biomni/tool/synthetic_biology.py#L1-L1352), [biomni/tool/database.py](biomni/tool/database.py#L16-L4975)

### Data Lake with Curated Datasets

On first initialization, Biomni downloads a **~11 GB data lake** containing over 80 curated datasets spanning protein interactions, gene expression, drug databases, GWAS catalogs, and more. These datasets are stored locally as Parquet, CSV, and Pickle files and are automatically referenced by tools during execution.

Key datasets include DepMap (cancer cell line dependencies), GTEx (tissue gene expression), GWAS Catalog, MSigDB gene sets, DisGeNET (gene-disease associations), BindingDB (drug-target binding), and drug-drug interaction databases from DDInter. Users can skip the download for faster testing by passing `expected_data_lake_files=[]`.

Sources: [biomni/env_desc.py](biomni/env_desc.py#L1-L80), [biomni/agent/a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L120-L150)

### Retrieval-Augmented Tool Selection

Rather than dumping every tool into the LLM context, Biomni uses a **Tool Retriever** powered by an LLM to intelligently select the most relevant tools, data lake files, software libraries, and know-how documents for each query. This keeps the context window manageable while ensuring the agent has access to everything it needs.

Sources: [biomni/model/retriever.py](biomni/model/retriever.py#L13-L70)

### Know-How Library

Biomni includes a curated **Know-How Library** — community-contributed markdown documents containing lab protocols, best practices, and troubleshooting guides. These are automatically loaded by the `KnowHowLoader`, indexed with metadata (authors, affiliations, licensing), and retrieved by the agent when relevant to the task at hand.

Sources: [biomni/know_how/loader.py](biomni/know_how/loader.py#L12-L100)

## Project Structure at a Glance

```
biomni/                      # Core Python package
├── agent/
│   ├── a1.py                # Main A1 agent class (entry point)
│   ├── react.py             # ReAct reasoning engine
│   └── function_generator.py # Tool function generation
├── config.py                # Centralized configuration (BiomniConfig)
├── model/
│   └── retriever.py         # LLM-based tool retrieval
├── tool/
│   ├── tool_registry.py     # Tool discovery and management
│   ├── support_tools.py     # Python REPL, plot capture
│   ├── database.py          # 30+ biomedical API integrations
│   ├── genomics.py          # Genomics analysis functions
│   ├── pharmacology.py      # Drug discovery & safety
│   ├── genetics.py          # Genetic analysis & CRISPR
│   ├── immunology.py        # Immunology & flow cytometry
│   ├── molecular_biology.py # Primer design, cloning, assembly
│   ├── synthetic_biology.py # Gene circuits, metabolic models
│   └── ... (14 more domains)
├── know_how/                # Know-how documents & loader
├── env_desc.py              # Data lake & library definitions
├── eval/                    # Benchmark evaluation (Biomni-Eval1)
└── task/                    # Task definitions (HLE, LabBench)

biomni_env/                  # Conda environment & setup scripts
tutorials/                   # Notebooks and examples
docs/                        # Documentation source
figs/                        # Branding assets
```

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L1-L421), [pyproject.toml](pyproject.toml#L1-L18)

## Key Design Principles

Biomni is built around three guiding principles that shape every architectural decision:

**Autonomous Reasoning over Templates.** Unlike workflow engines that require predefined pipelines, Biomni uses LLM-based ReAct reasoning to dynamically plan and adapt its approach. The agent decides which tools to use, in what order, and how to interpret results — all from a natural language description of the task.

**Retrieval-Augmented Efficiency.** With thousands of available tools and dozens of datasets, naively loading everything into the LLM context would be infeasible. The Tool Retriever solves this by using a secondary LLM call to filter resources down to the most relevant subset before the main reasoning loop begins.

**Extensibility by Design.** Every component — tools, datasets, know-how documents, MCP servers, and even LLM providers — can be added, removed, or replaced without modifying the core agent logic. New tools are registered by decorating Python functions with metadata; new datasets are added to the data lake dictionary; new LLM providers are configured through the `source` parameter.

Sources: [biomni/agent/a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L46-L80), [biomni/model/retriever.py](biomni/model/retriever.py#L13-L70), [biomni/tool/tool_registry.py](biomni/tool/tool_registry.py#L13-L50)

## Ecosystem Highlights

Beyond the core agent, the Biomni ecosystem includes two significant research artifacts:

**Biomni-R0** — A 32B-parameter reasoning model fine-tuned with reinforcement learning from agent interaction data. Built on Qwen-32B, it excels at multi-step biological reasoning and tool use. It can be served locally via SGLang and used as the agent's reasoning LLM while keeping database queries on a separate provider.

**Biomni-Eval1** — A benchmark with 433 instances across 10 biological reasoning tasks, including GWAS causal gene identification, rare disease diagnosis, patient gene detection, and CRISPR delivery method selection. It provides a standardized way to evaluate biomedical AI agents.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L310-L370), [biomni/eval/biomni_eval1.py](biomni/eval/biomni_eval1.py)

## Important Notes

Biomni executes LLM-generated code with **full system privileges**. In production settings, always run it in isolated or sandboxed environments. The agent can access files, networks, and system commands. Additionally, while the Biomni framework itself is Apache 2.0-licensed, some integrated tools, databases, and datasets carry more restrictive commercial licenses. The `commercial_mode` configuration flag automatically filters out non-commercial datasets for compliance.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L400-L421), [biomni/config.py](biomni/config.py#L30-L35)

# Quick Start



Get Biomni running in under ten minutes. This guide walks you through environment setup, package installation, API key configuration, and your first biomedical AI agent invocation — each step verified against the actual codebase.

![Biomni Logo](https://github.com/snap-stanford/Biomni/blob/main/figs/biomni_logo.png?raw=true)

## Architecture at a Glance

Before diving into installation, it helps to understand the three-layer architecture you are setting up. The diagram below shows the dependency flow from your Python code down to the execution environment.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Your Application"
        A["from biomni.agent import A1"]
        B["agent.go('your task')"]
    end

    subgraph "Biomni Agent Core"
        C["A1.__init__()"]
        D["LangGraph ReAct Loop"]
        E["Tool Registry + Retriever"]
        F["Know-How Loader"]
    end

    subgraph "Data Layer"
        G["Data Lake<br/>~11 GB auto-download"]
        H["Know-How Library<br/>Domain documents"]
    end

    subgraph "Execution Environment"
        I["Conda: biomni_e1<br/>Python 3.11"]
        J["Python REPL<br/>R Runtime<br/>Bioinformatics CLI tools"]
    end

    A --> C
    C --> D
    C --> E
    C --> F
    C --> G
    C --> H
    D --> J
    B --> D

    style A fill:#4A90D9,color:#fff
    style I fill:#2ECC71,color:#fff
```

The **Agent Core** (layer 2) is what you install via pip. The **Execution Environment** (layer 3) is what you install via conda — it provides the Python 3.11 runtime, bioinformatics tools, and R packages that the agent's code executor calls into at runtime. The **Data Layer** is downloaded automatically on first run.

Sources: [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L56-L68), [pyproject.toml](pyproject.toml#L13-L18)

---

## Prerequisites

Biomni requires a specific stack. Make sure you have these before proceeding.

| Requirement | Minimum Version | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| **Conda** (or Micromamba) | Any recent version | Environment management for the execution layer |
| **Python** | 3.11 | Runtime for the Biomni package itself |
| **LLM API Key** | — | Anthropic (Claude), OpenAI, or another supported provider |
| **Disk Space** | ~30 GB (full), ~13 GB (reduced) | For the conda environment and data lake downloads |
| **OS** | Ubuntu 22.04 64-bit (tested) | The full `setup.sh` script is validated on this platform |

Sources: [pyproject.toml](pyproject.toml#L17), [biomni_env/README.md](biomni_env/README.md#L1-L75)

---

## Step 1 — Set Up the Execution Environment

Biomni ships four environment options, each representing a different trade-off between completeness and setup time. Choose the one that matches your needs:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Which environment?"] --> B{"Need full<br/>tool support?"}
    B -- "Yes" --> C["setup.sh<br/>>10 hours, ~30 GB"]
    B -- "No" --> D{"Need bio tools<br/>without R/CLI?"}
    D -- "Yes" --> E["fixed_env.yml<br/>~13 GB"]
    D -- "No" --> F{"Just want to<br/>try the agent?"}
    F -- "Yes" --> G["environment.yml<br/>Minimal, fast"]
    F -- "Specific need" --> H["bio_env_py310.yml<br/>Copy number analysis"]
```

### Option A — Full Environment (all tools, R, CLI)

This is the recommended option for production use. Clone the repository and run the setup script inside the `biomni_env/` directory.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/snap-stanford/Biomni.git
cd Biomni/biomni_env
bash setup.sh
```

The script is interactive — it will prompt you to confirm each optional component. The full installation takes over 10 hours and requires at least 30 GB of free disk space. It installs conda packages, R packages, and bioinformatics CLI tools (BLAST, Bowtie2, BWA, FastQC, MAFFT, and more) via the [install_cli_tools.sh](biomni_env/install_cli_tools.sh) script.

Sources: [setup.sh](biomni_env/setup.sh#L1-L80), [biomni_env/README.md](biomni_env/README.md#L20-L28)

### Option B — Reduced Environment (bio tools, no R/CLI)

A middle ground that includes most scientific Python packages and bioinformatics libraries from both `environment.yml` and `bio_env.yml`, but skips R and CLI tool installations. Requires approximately 13 GB.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/snap-stanford/Biomni.git
cd Biomni/biomni_env
conda env create -f fixed_env.yml
```

This environment includes pre-pinned versions of over 200 conda packages including Biopython, bedtools, BLAST, bowtie2, BWA, diamond, entrez-direct, FastQC, gseapy, htslib, MAFFT, and pandas — all with exact version pins for reproducibility.

Sources: [fixed_env.yml](biomni_env/fixed_env.yml#L1-L40), [biomni_env/README.md](biomni_env/README.md#L31-L37)

### Option C — Minimal Environment (agent only)

The fastest path to a working agent. This installs only the Python packages needed to run the A1 agent core — no bioinformatics tools.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/snap-stanford/Biomni.git
cd Biomni/biomni_env
conda env create -f environment.yml
```

Sources: [biomni_env/README.md](biomni_env/README.md#L15-L19), [environment.yml](biomni_env/environment.yml#L1-L40)

### Activate the Environment

Regardless of which option you chose, activate it before proceeding:

```bash
conda activate biomni_e1
```

Sources: [biomni_env/README.md](biomni_env/README.md#L43-L45)

---

## Step 2 — Install the Biomni Package

With the conda environment active, install the Biomni Python package. Two options are available:

```bash
# Option 1: PyPI release (stable)
pip install biomni --upgrade

# Option 2: Latest from GitHub main branch
pip install git+https://github.com/snap-stanford/Biomni.git@main
```

The package installs three core dependencies: **pydantic**, **langchain**, and **python-dotenv**. All other dependencies (numpy, pandas, scipy, etc.) are provided by the conda environment you created in Step 1.

> [!TIP]
> The package version is currently `0.0.8`. If you install from GitHub, you always get the latest main-branch code, which may include features and fixes not yet released to PyPI.

Sources: [pyproject.toml](pyproject.toml#L1-L21), [version.py](biomni/version.py#L1-L2)

---

## Step 3 — Configure Your API Key

Biomni needs access to an LLM provider. The A1 constructor automatically loads a `.env` file if one exists in your working directory. The simplest approach:

Create a `.env` file in your project directory with at least one provider key:

```env
# Required for Claude models (recommended)
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-xxxxxxxxxxxx

# Optional: for OpenAI models
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-xxxxxxxxxxxx
```

Alternatively, export environment variables directly in your shell:

```bash
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="sk-ant-xxxxxxxxxxxx"
```

The agent auto-detects which provider to use based on the model name prefix you pass to the constructor — `claude-` routes to Anthropic, `gpt-` routes to OpenAI, `gemini-` routes to Google, and so on. This detection logic lives in the `get_llm()` function in [biomni/llm.py](biomni/llm.py#L1-L276).

For the complete list of supported providers and advanced configuration (Azure, Bedrock, Groq, Ollama, custom endpoints), see [API Key Configuration](3-api-key-configuration).

Sources: [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L47-L50), [config.py](biomni/config.py#L1-L100)

---

## Step 4 — Run Your First Task

You are now ready to invoke the agent. The following code initializes A1, downloads the data lake (on first run only), and executes a biomedical task using natural language.

```python
from biomni.agent import A1

# Initialize the agent
# First run: ~11 GB data lake files are downloaded automatically
agent = A1(path='./data', llm='claude-sonnet-4-20250514')

# Execute a biomedical task
agent.go("Plan a CRISPR screen to identify genes that regulate T cell exhaustion, generate 32 genes that maximize the perturbation effect.")
```

### What Happens When You Initialize A1

The constructor performs several setup steps in sequence. Understanding this flow helps with troubleshooting.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant You
    participant A1 as A1.__init__()
    participant FS as File System
    participant S3 as AWS S3
    participant LLM as LLM Provider

    You->>A1: A1(path='./data', llm='claude-sonnet-4-...')
    A1->>A1: Load default_config values
    A1->>A1: Load env_desc (data lake dict + library dict)
    A1->>FS: Create ./data/biomni_data/ directories
    A1->>S3: Check & download missing data lake files (~11 GB)
    A1->>S3: Check & download benchmark files (if missing)
    A1->>LLM: Initialize LLM client via get_llm()
    A1->>A1: Initialize ToolRegistry + ToolRetriever
    A1->>A1: Initialize KnowHowLoader
    A1->>A1: configure() — build system prompt + LangGraph workflow
    A1-->>You: Agent ready
```

### Constructor Parameters Reference

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | `str` | `"./data"` | Root directory for data lake storage |
| `llm` | `str` | `"claude-sonnet-4-5"` | Model name (auto-detects provider from prefix) |
| `source` | `str` | `None` (auto-detect) | Explicit provider: `"OpenAI"`, `"Anthropic"`, `"Gemini"`, etc. |
| `use_tool_retriever` | `bool` | `True` | Enable retrieval-augmented tool selection |
| `timeout_seconds` | `int` | `600` | Code execution timeout per step |
| `commercial_mode` | `bool` | `False` | If `True`, excludes non-commercial datasets |
| `expected_data_lake_files` | `list` | `None` (all files) | Pass `[]` to skip data lake download |

Sources: [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L56-L68), [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L130-L180)

### More Task Examples

Biomni spans a wide range of biomedical domains. Here are examples that exercise different tool sets:

```python
# Single-cell RNA-seq annotation
agent.go("Perform scRNA-seq annotation at /path/to/data.h5ad and generate meaningful hypothesis")

# Drug property prediction
agent.go("Predict ADMET properties for this compound: CC(C)CC1=CC=C(C=C1)C(C)C(=O)O")

# Literature and database queries
agent.go("Find FDA-approved drugs targeting the EGFR pathway with their mechanism of action")

# Genomic analysis
agent.go("Identify potential causal genes for the GWAS lead variant rs12345 near BRCA1 locus")
```

---

## Step 5 — Skip Data Lake Download (Optional)

If you want to iterate quickly during development, or if you are working in a bandwidth-limited environment, you can skip the ~11 GB automatic data lake download:

```python
agent = A1(path='./data', llm='claude-sonnet-4-20250514', expected_data_lake_files=[])
```

This initializes the agent with only the in-memory tool registry and know-how library. Some tools that depend on specific data files (e.g., pre-built indexes, reference genomes) will not function without their corresponding data lake entries.

> [!TIP]
> Use `expected_data_lake_files=[]` for rapid prototyping and testing of the agent's reasoning loop. Switch back to the default (full download) when you need the complete tool ecosystem.

Sources: [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L160-L175)

---

## Step 6 — Launch the Web Interface (Optional)

Biomni includes a built-in Gradio web UI for interactive, no-code usage. Install the Gradio dependency and launch:

```bash
# Install Gradio (requires 5.x, not 6.x)
pip install "gradio>=5.0,<6.0"
```

```python
from biomni.agent import A1

agent = A1(path='./data', llm='claude-sonnet-4-20250514')
agent.launch_gradio_demo()
```

The interface becomes available at `http://localhost:7860`. Key options:

| Parameter | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `share` | `False` | Create a public shareable Gradio link |
| `server_name` | `"0.0.0.0"` | Bind address; use `"127.0.0.1"` for localhost-only |
| `require_verification` | `False` | Require access code (default: `"Biomni2025"`) |

For more details on the web interface, see [Gradio Web Interface](4-gradio-web-interface).

Sources: [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L2627-L2650), [README.md](README.md#L1-L200)

---

## Streaming Execution

For long-running tasks or when you need real-time visibility into the agent's reasoning steps, use `go_stream()` instead of `go()`. It returns a generator that yields each step as a dictionary:

```python
for step in agent.go_stream("Identify druggable targets in the Wnt signaling pathway"):
    print(step["output"])
```

This is particularly useful when building your own front-end or logging system on top of Biomni. Both `go()` and `go_stream()` share the same LangGraph workflow — the difference is purely in how results are delivered to your code.

Sources: [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L1791-L1828)

---

## Troubleshooting Common Issues

| Symptom | Likely Cause | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| `ImportError: langchain-openai` | Missing langchain provider package | `pip install langchain-openai` or `langchain-anthropic` |
| `ImportError: Gradio is not installed` | Gradio not in environment | `pip install "gradio>=5.0,<6.0"` |
| Data lake download stalls | Network issues or S3 timeout | Use `expected_data_lake_files=[]` to skip, retry later |
| `gpt-5` model returns 400 error | Responses API incompatibility | Handled automatically in code — ensure latest pip version |
| Tool X not found at runtime | Tool requires data lake file | Ensure data lake fully downloaded (remove `expected_data_lake_files=[]`) |
| Conda env creation fails | Package conflicts | Try `fixed_env.yml` instead of full `setup.sh` |

For a complete list of known package conflicts (hyperimpute, langchain_aws, cnvkit, panhumanpy), see [docs/known_conflicts.md](docs/known_conflicts.md).

Sources: [known_conflicts.md](docs/known_conflicts.md#L1-L35)

- **[API Key Configuration](3-api-key-configuration)** — Configure multiple providers, Azure, Bedrock, Ollama, and custom model endpoints
- **[Gradio Web Interface](4-gradio-web-interface)** — Full guide to deploying the interactive UI with authentication

# API Key Configuration



![Biomni Logo](https://github.com/snap-stanford/Biomni/blob/main/figs/biomni_logo.png?raw=true)

Biomni communicates with external LLM providers and third-party services through API keys. This page explains exactly which keys you need, where the code reads them from, and how to configure them step by step — so you can get the agent running without guessing.

## Where API Keys Enter the System

Before diving into specific keys, it helps to understand the loading pipeline. Biomni uses a layered configuration system with three tiers of priority:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[".env file<br/>(project root)"] --> D{Priority Merge}
    B["Shell environment<br/>variables"] --> D
    C["BiomniConfig<br/>Python object"] --> D
    D --> E["BiomniConfig.__post_init__<br/>env var overrides"]
    E --> F["get_llm() function<br/>reads provider keys"]
    F --> G["Agent & Database tools<br/>use resolved config"]

    style A fill:#4CAF50,color:#fff
    style B fill:#2196F3,color:#fff
    style C fill:#FF9800,color:#fff
    style G fill:#9C27B0,color:#fff
```

The entry point is the `A1` agent class in [biomni/agent/a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L46-L48), which calls `load_dotenv(".env")` on initialization. Then `BiomniConfig.__post_init__()` in [biomni/config.py](biomni/config.py#L55-L81) checks for environment variable overrides and applies them. Finally, `get_llm()` in [biomni/llm.py](biomni/llm.py#L13-L21) reads the provider-specific API key (e.g., `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`) directly from `os.environ` at model instantiation time.

**Priority order**: Constructor parameters > Runtime `default_config` modifications > Environment variables > Hardcoded defaults. This means if you set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in both `.env` and `~/.bashrc`, the `.env` file value wins (it is loaded first and `override=False` is used).
Sources: [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L46-L48), [config.py](biomni/config.py#L55-L81), [llm.py](biomni/llm.py#L13-L21)

## Supported LLM Providers and Their API Keys

Biomni supports eight LLM sources. Each one requires a different API key. The table below maps every supported provider to its required environment variable, the default model, and which LangChain package it depends on.

| Provider | `source` value | Required Env Var | Default Model | Required Package |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Anthropic** | `"Anthropic"` | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | `claude-sonnet-4-5` | `langchain-anthropic` |
| **OpenAI** | `"OpenAI"` | `OPENAI_API_KEY` | — | `langchain-openai` |
| **Azure OpenAI** | `"AzureOpenAI"` | `OPENAI_API_KEY` + `OPENAI_ENDPOINT` | — (prefix `azure-`) | `langchain-openai` |
| **Google Gemini** | `"Gemini"` | `GEMINI_API_KEY` | — | `langchain-openai` |
| **Groq** | `"Groq"` | `GROQ_API_KEY` | — | `langchain-openai` |
| **AWS Bedrock** | `"Bedrock"` | `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` + `AWS_REGION` | — | `langchain-aws` |
| **Ollama (local)** | `"Ollama"` | *None* | — | `langchain-ollama` |
| **Custom endpoint** | `"Custom"` | `BIOMNI_CUSTOM_API_KEY` + `BIOMNI_CUSTOM_BASE_URL` | — | `langchain-openai` |

The `SourceType` literal in [biomni/llm.py](biomni/llm.py#L9-L10) defines the exact set of valid source strings. If you don't specify a source, `get_llm()` auto-detects it from the model name prefix — for example, models starting with `claude-` route to Anthropic, models starting with `gpt-` route to OpenAI, and models containing `groq` route to Groq.
Sources: [llm.py](biomni/llm.py#L56-L95)

## Method 1: The `.env` File (Recommended)

Create a `.env` file in your **project root directory** (the same folder where you run your Python scripts). The A1 agent automatically loads this file on startup via `load_dotenv()`.

```bash
# .env — place in your project root

# ─── REQUIRED: At least one LLM provider key ───────────────
# Anthropic Claude (default model for Biomni)
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-xxxxx

# OpenAI (if you want to use GPT models)
# OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-xxxxx

# ─── OPTIONAL: Other LLM providers ─────────────────────────
# GEMINI_API_KEY=AIzaxxxxx
# GROQ_API_KEY=gsk_xxxxx
# AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK=xxxxx
# AWS_REGION=us-east-1

# Azure OpenAI (requires both key and endpoint)
# OPENAI_ENDPOINT=https://your-resource.openai.azure.com/

# ─── OPTIONAL: Force a specific provider ───────────────────
# LLM_SOURCE=Anthropic

# ─── OPTIONAL: Custom/self-hosted model serving ────────────
# BIOMNI_CUSTOM_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8000/v1
# BIOMNI_CUSTOM_API_KEY=your_key

# ─── OPTIONAL: Protocols.io integration ────────────────────
# PROTOCOLS_IO_ACCESS_TOKEN=your_token
```

> [!TIP]
> Only **one** LLM provider key is strictly required. Since Biomni defaults to `claude-sonnet-4-5`, setting `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` alone is sufficient to get started. Add other keys only when you want to switch providers or use multiple models.

The `.env` file is loaded with `override=False`, meaning environment variables already present in the shell will **not** be overwritten. This is intentional — it lets your CI/CD pipeline set keys at the container level while still allowing local `.env` overrides during development. Source: [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L46-L48)

## Method 2: Shell Environment Variables

If you prefer to set keys globally (e.g., for use across multiple projects), add exports to your shell profile:

```bash
# Add to ~/.bashrc or ~/.zshrc
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="sk-ant-xxxxx"
export OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-xxxxx"          # optional
export GEMINI_API_KEY="AIzaxxxxx"         # optional
export GROQ_API_KEY="gsk_xxxxx"           # optional
export AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK="xxxxx"   # optional
export AWS_REGION="us-east-1"             # optional for Bedrock
export OPENAI_ENDPOINT="https://your-resource.openai.azure.com/"  # Azure only
```

After editing, reload your profile with `source ~/.bashrc` (or restart your terminal). Verify the key is loaded:

```bash
echo $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
```

For Anthropic specifically, Biomni has a **fallback mechanism**: if `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is not found in the environment when an Anthropic model is requested, the code in [biomni/llm.py](biomni/llm.py#L168-L182) attempts to source it from `~/.bash_profile` via a subprocess call. This provides an extra safety net but is not reliable for all shell configurations. Source: [llm.py](biomni/llm.py#L168-L182)

## Method 3: Python Runtime Configuration

You can also configure API keys and model settings directly in Python code. This approach is useful for scripting and testing.

```python
from biomni.config import BiomniConfig, default_config

# Modify the global default config (affects all agents created after this point)
default_config.llm = "gpt-4"
default_config.source = "OpenAI"
default_config.temperature = 0.5
```

For **custom model serving** (e.g., SGLang, vLLM, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint), you must set both `base_url` and `api_key` on the config object. These are the only fields on `BiomniConfig` that directly hold an API key value — all other providers read their keys from environment variables. Source: [config.py](biomni/config.py#L46-L47)

```python
from biomni.config import default_config

# Custom local model (e.g., served by Ollama, SGLang, or vLLM)
default_config.source = "Custom"
default_config.base_url = "http://localhost:8000/v1"
default_config.api_key = "local_key"       # Only used for Custom source
default_config.llm = "Llama-3-70B-Instruct"

from biomni.agent import A1
agent = A1()
```

> [!TIP]
> The `api_key` field on `BiomniConfig` is **only** used when `source` is set to `"Custom"`. For all other providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, etc.), the key is read from the corresponding environment variable (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, etc.) — **not** from this config field. This is a common source of confusion for beginners.

## Third-Party Service Keys

Beyond LLM providers, one additional service requires an API key:

### Protocols.io Access Token

The protocols integration in [biomni/tool/protocols.py](biomni/tool/protocols.py#L24-L26) reads a bearer token to search and retrieve biological protocols. The token is resolved in this priority order:

1. `PROTOCOLS_IO_ACCESS_TOKEN` environment variable
2. `BIOMNI_PROTOCOLS_IO_ACCESS_TOKEN` environment variable
3. `BiomniConfig.protocols_io_access_token` Python attribute

```bash
# In your .env or shell profile
PROTOCOLS_IO_ACCESS_TOKEN=your_token_here
```

Or in Python:

```python
from biomni.config import default_config
default_config.protocols_io_access_token = "your_token_here"
```

Without this token, protocol search tools will raise a `ValueError` at runtime but will not prevent the agent from starting. Source: [protocols.py](biomni/tool/protocols.py#L24-L26)

## Advanced: Web Search with Anthropic API

The `advanced_web_search_claude()` function in [biomni/tool/literature.py](biomni/tool/literature.py#L246-L262) uses Anthropic's native web search tool via the `anthropic` Python SDK directly (not through LangChain). It reads the API key from `BiomniConfig.api_key`, falling back to the `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` environment variable. This feature requires a **Claude model** specifically and will raise a `ValueError` if a non-Claude model is configured. Source: [literature.py](biomni/tool/literature.py#L246-L262)

## All Environment Variables Reference

The following table lists every environment variable that Biomni reads for API key and model configuration purposes, grouped by category.

### LLM Provider Keys

| Variable | Used By | Required? | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | `get_llm()` for Anthropic models | Yes (default model) | — |
| `OPENAI_API_KEY` | `get_llm()` for OpenAI/Azure models | Only if using OpenAI | — |
| `OPENAI_ENDPOINT` | `get_llm()` for Azure OpenAI | Only if using Azure | — |
| `GEMINI_API_KEY` | `get_llm()` for Gemini models | Only if using Gemini | — |
| `GROQ_API_KEY` | `get_llm()` for Groq models | Only if using Groq | — |
| `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` | `get_llm()` for Bedrock models | Only if using Bedrock | — |
| `AWS_REGION` | `get_llm()` for Bedrock models | Only if using Bedrock | `us-east-1` |

### Model Source Override

| Variable | Used By | Required? | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `LLM_SOURCE` | `get_llm()` auto-detection override | No | Auto-detect from model name |

### Custom Model Serving

| Variable | Used By | Required? | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `BIOMNI_CUSTOM_BASE_URL` | `BiomniConfig.__post_init__()` | Only for Custom source | `None` |
| `BIOMNI_CUSTOM_API_KEY` | `BiomniConfig.__post_init__()` | Only for Custom source | `None` |

### Third-Party Integrations

| Variable | Used By | Required? | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PROTOCOLS_IO_ACCESS_TOKEN` | `protocols.py` module-level | Only for protocol search | `None` |
| `BIOMNI_PROTOCOLS_IO_ACCESS_TOKEN` | `protocols.py` (alternate name) | Only for protocol search | `None` |

### Biomni Behavioral Settings

| Variable | Used By | Required? | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `BIOMNI_LLM` / `BIOMNI_LLM_MODEL` | `BiomniConfig.__post_init__()` | No | `claude-sonnet-4-5` |
| `BIOMNI_TEMPERATURE` | `BiomniConfig.__post_init__()` | No | `0.7` |
| `BIOMNI_PATH` / `BIOMNI_DATA_PATH` | `BiomniConfig.__post_init__()` | No | `./data` |
| `BIOMNI_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | `BiomniConfig.__post_init__()` | No | `600` |
| `BIOMNI_USE_TOOL_RETRIEVER` | `BiomniConfig.__post_init__()` | No | `true` |
| `BIOMNI_COMMERCIAL_MODE` | `BiomniConfig.__post_init__()` | No | `false` |
| `BIOMNI_SOURCE` | `BiomniConfig.__post_init__()` | No | `None` (auto-detect) |

Sources: [config.py](biomni/config.py#L55-L81), [llm.py](biomni/llm.py#L56-L95), [protocols.py](biomni/tool/protocols.py#L24-L26)

## Troubleshooting Common Issues

| Symptom | Likely Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `Unable to determine model source` | Model name not recognized and no `source`/`LLM_SOURCE` set | Set `LLM_SOURCE` explicitly, or use a recognized model prefix (`claude-`, `gpt-`, `gemini-`, etc.) |
| `base_url must be provided for customly served LLMs` | Using `source="Custom"` without setting `base_url` | Set `BIOMNI_CUSTOM_BASE_URL` or `default_config.base_url` |
| `anthropic` package not found errors | Missing `langchain-anthropic` dependency | Install with `pip install langchain-anthropic` |
| Agent starts but protocol search fails | Missing `PROTOCOLS_IO_ACCESS_TOKEN` | Set the token in `.env` or via `default_config.protocols_io_access_token` |
| `.env` keys appear ignored | `.env` file in wrong directory | Ensure `.env` is in the **working directory** where you run Python, not in the package directory |

## Quick Start Checklist

Follow these steps in order to configure your API keys:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["1. Create .env file<br/>in project root"] --> B["2. Set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY<br/>(or your preferred provider)"]
    B --> C["3. Verify: echo $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"]
    C --> D["4. pip install the provider<br/>package (e.g. langchain-anthropic)"]
    D --> E["5. from biomni.agent import A1<br/>agent = A1()"]
    E --> F{Agent starts?}
    F -->|Yes| G["✅ Ready to go!"]
    F -->|No| H["Check error message<br/>against troubleshooting table"]
    H --> B

    style A fill:#4CAF50,color:#fff
    style G fill:#4CAF50,color:#fff
```

Now that your API keys are configured, you can:

- **Launch the agent**: Head to [Quick Start](2-quick-start) for your first biomedical task
- **Try the web interface**: See [Gradio Web Interface](4-gradio-web-interface) for the interactive UI
- **Fine-tune model selection**: Explore cost optimization with different models for agent reasoning vs. database queries in [Configuration Reference](21-configuration-reference)
- **Switch providers**: Learn about all eight supported LLM sources in [Architecture Overview](8-architecture-overview)

# Gradio Web Interface



The Gradio web interface provides a fully interactive, no-code way to converse with the Biomni A1 agent directly from your browser. Rather than writing Python scripts and calling `agent.go()` in a loop, you get a dual-panel chat environment where the agent reasons, executes code, and returns results in real time — all streamed live into your browser window. This page walks you through every step of launching, configuring, and using the interface.

![Biomni Logo](https://github.com/snap-stanford/Biomni/blob/main/figs/biomni_logo.png?raw=true)

## Architecture Overview

The Gradio interface wraps the same `A1` agent you use programmatically, but adds a browser-based UX layer on top. Understanding how these pieces connect helps you troubleshoot and customize effectively.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph Browser["🌐 Browser (Gradio UI)"]
        MainChat["Main Chatbot<br/>Conversation & Answers"]
        InnerChat["Executor Chatbot<br/>Reasoning & Code"]
        FileUpload["File Upload<br/>(.png, .jpg, .pdf, etc.)"]
        Verification["Access Verification<br/>(optional)"]
    end

    subgraph A1Agent["🧠 A1 Agent (biomni.agent.A1)"]
        LLM["LLM Reasoning<br/>(Claude, GPT, etc.)"]
        ReAct["ReAct Engine<br/>(Think → Act → Observe)"]
        ToolRetriever["Tool Retriever<br/>(optional)"]
        REPL["Python/Bash/R REPL"]
        DataLake["Data Lake<br/>(~11GB)"]
    end

    FileUpload -->|"User prompt + files"| MainChat
    Verification -->|"Access code check"| MainChat
    MainChat -->|"generate_response()"| ReAct
    ReAct -->|"Streaming messages"| InnerChat
    ReAct --> LLM
    ReAct --> ToolRetriever
    ToolRetriever --> DataLake
    ReAct --> REPL
    REPL -->|"Observations & files"| InnerChat
    InnerChat -->|"✅ Solution"| MainChat
```

When you type a question and press Enter, the `generate_response()` function inside [`launch_gradio_demo()`](biomni/agent/a1.py#L2627) takes over. It converts your message into LangChain `HumanMessage` objects, feeds them into the agent's LangGraph workflow, and streams every intermediate step — reasoning thoughts, code blocks, execution outputs, and final answers — back to the two chat panels.

Sources: [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L2627-L3002), [pyproject.toml](pyproject.toml#L28-L29)

## Prerequisites

Before launching the interface, you need three things in place: the Biomni environment, the pip package, and an API key. If you have already completed the [Quick Start](2-quick-start) guide, you can skip ahead to [Installing Gradio](#installing-gradio).

| Requirement | Purpose | How to Verify |
|---|---|---|
| Conda environment `biomni_e1` | Provides R, Bash, and scientific tools the agent may invoke | `conda activate biomni_e1` |
| `biomni` pip package | The core agent library | `pip show biomni` |
| API key (e.g., Anthropic) | Powers the LLM behind the agent | Check your `.env` file or `echo $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` |

If you haven't set up the environment yet, follow the instructions in [biomni_env/README.md](biomni_env/README.md) first, then install the package:

```bash
conda activate biomni_e1
pip install biomni --upgrade
```

For API key configuration, see the [API Key Configuration](3-api-key-configuration) page for detailed instructions on setting up Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, Groq, or custom model providers.

## Installing Gradio

Biomni requires **Gradio 5.x** specifically. Gradio 6.0 introduced breaking API changes that are incompatible with the current interface implementation. Install it as an optional dependency:

```bash
pip install "gradio>=5.0,<6.0"
```

This exact version constraint is declared in the project's [`pyproject.toml`](pyproject.toml#L28-L29) under `[project.optional-dependencies]`. If you accidentally have Gradio 6.x installed, the interface will throw attribute errors at runtime — in that case, downgrade with:

```bash
pip install "gradio>=5.0,<6.0" --force-reinstall
```

> [!TIP]
> If you encounter `ImportError: Gradio is not installed` when calling `launch_gradio_demo()`, the function itself catches this and raises a clear error message directing you to the correct pip command. This guard is implemented at [line 2640–2644 of a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L2640-L2644).

## Launching the Interface

The minimal launch requires just two lines of Python:

```python
from biomni.agent import A1

agent = A1(path='./data', llm='claude-sonnet-4-20250514')
agent.launch_gradio_demo()
```

After running this, you will see output like:

```
Launching Gradio demo on 0.0.0.0:7860
Running on local URL:  http://0.0.0.0:7860
```

Open **http://localhost:7860** in your browser to see the interface.

The [`launch_gradio_demo()`](biomni/agent/a1.py#L2627) method accepts four parameters that control how the server behaves:

| Parameter | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `thread_id` | `42` | Conversation thread ID for the agent's internal memory. Each unique thread maintains separate conversation history. |
| `share` | `False` | Creates a temporary public Gradio share link (e.g., `https://xxxx.gradio.live`). Useful for demos but not for production. |
| `server_name` | `"0.0.0.0"` | Network binding. Use `"127.0.0.1"` for local-only access (more secure), or `"0.0.0.0"` to allow connections from other machines on your network. |
| `require_verification` | `False` | When `True`, displays an access code entry screen before the main interface. Default code is `"Biomni2025"`. |

Here are common launch patterns depending on your use case:

```python
# Local-only development (most secure)
agent.launch_gradio_demo(server_name="127.0.0.1")

# Share with a colleague via public link
agent.launch_gradio_demo(share=True)

# Deploy on a server with access control
agent.launch_gradio_demo(server_name="0.0.0.0", require_verification=True)
```

Sources: [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L2627-L2639), [README.md](README.md#L143-L160)

## Interface Layout

The Gradio UI uses a dual-panel design built with `gr.Blocks()` and two side-by-side `gr.Chatbot` components, both set to `type="messages"` for rich message rendering. This layout is defined at [lines 2946–2997 of a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L2946-L2997).

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph Left["Left Panel — Biomni A1 Agent"]
        A1["💬 Main conversation"]
        A1Q["User questions"]
        A1A["✅ Final answers"]
        A1C["📝 Summaries"]
    end

    subgraph Right["Right Panel — Biomni Executor"]
        EX1["🤔 Reasoning<br/>(agent's thinking)"]
        EX2["🛠️ Executing code...<br/>(Python / R / Bash)"]
        EX3["Observation<br/>(execution output)"]
        EX4["📁 Files<br/>(images, PDFs)"]
        EX5["🔄 Complete<br/>(return to main)"]
    end

    A1Q -->|"generates"| EX1
    EX1 --> EX2
    EX2 --> EX3
    EX3 --> EX4
    EX5 --> A1A
```

### Main Chatbot (Left Panel)

The **left panel** is your primary conversation partner. It shows your questions (as user messages) and the agent's **final answers** (marked with ✅). This is where you read the cleaned-up, human-readable results. If the agent doesn't produce a formal `<solution>` tag, it falls back to a cleaned summary (marked with 📝) instead.

### Executor Chatbot (Right Panel)

The **right panel** is the agent's "workbench." It streams every intermediate step in real time:

| Step | Icon | What You See |
|---|---|---|
| Reasoning | 🤔 | The agent's thinking text before any code execution |
| Code execution | 🛠️ | Syntax-highlighted code blocks (Python, R, or Bash) with a "pending" status indicator |
| Observation | — | Raw execution output, collapsible by default |
| File previews | 📁/🖼️/📄 | Automatically detected images and PDFs from execution output |
| Completion | 🔄 | A "Returning the result to the main interface…" message |

At the bottom of the interface sits a **multimodal text input** that accepts both typed text and file uploads. Supported file extensions are: `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.gif`, `.bmp`, `.webp`, and `.pdf` — defined as [`SUPPORTED_EXTENSIONS`](biomni/agent/a1.py#L2650) inside the method. Uploaded files are passed to the agent with an appended note: `"User uploaded this file: {path}. Please use it if needed."`

Sources: [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L2649-L2650), [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L2668-L2687), [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L2946-L2997)

## How Streaming Works

The interface uses Python generators (`yield`) to stream updates to both chat panels as the agent works. The [`generate_response()`](biomni/agent/a1.py#L2668) function processes the agent's output message by message, parsing three XML-style tags that the agent emits during its reasoning loop:

**`<reasoning>`** — Free-text thinking that appears before any action. Extracted by finding text preceding the first action tag ([lines 2747–2766](biomni/agent/a1.py#L2747-L2766)).

**`<execute>...</execute>`** — Code blocks the agent wants to run. The parser detects shebang lines (`#!R`, `#!BASH`, `#!CLI`) to determine the execution language ([lines 2784–2807](biomni/agent/a1.py#L2784-L2807)).

**`<observation>...</observation>`** — The output returned after code execution, which may contain file paths for automatic image/PDF preview ([lines 2810–2895](biomni/agent/a1.py#L2810-L2895)).

**`<solution>...</solution>`** — The agent's final answer, which gets routed to the main chatbot panel ([lines 2769–2781](biomni/agent/a1.py#L2769-L2781)).

Each `yield` call pushes updated chat histories to both panels simultaneously, so you see reasoning appear on the right while the left panel waits for the final answer.

Sources: [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L2736-L2897), [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L2899-L2939)

## Access Verification

When you enable verification by passing `require_verification=True`, the interface first shows a locked screen with a password input. Only users who enter a valid access code can see the main chat interface.

The default access code is `"Biomni2025"`, stored in the [`available_access_codes`](biomni/agent/a1.py#L2655) list. The verification logic at [lines 2658–2666](biomni/agent/a1.py#L2658-L2666) checks the entered code against this list and either reveals the main interface or displays an error message.

This is useful when you deploy the interface on a shared server or a cloud instance with `server_name="0.0.0.0"`, preventing unauthorized access. Note that the access codes are currently hardcoded — for production deployments, you should modify this list or add your own authentication layer.

Sources: [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L2654-L2666)

## File Upload and Preview

The interface supports uploading multiple files at once through the `gr.MultimodalTextbox` component. Here's how uploaded files flow through the system:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Upload["📁 User uploads file"] --> Append["Text appended:<br/>'User uploaded this file: path'"]
    Append --> Agent["Agent receives full prompt"]
    Agent --> Code["Agent writes code<br/>that reads the file"]
    Code --> Obs["Observation contains<br/>file output paths"]
    Obs --> Detect["Regex scans for<br/>.png .jpg .pdf etc."]
    Detect --> Valid["Valid local paths?"]
    Valid -->|"Yes"| Preview["🖼️ Image or 📄 PDF<br/>rendered in Executor panel"]
    Valid -->|"No"| Skip["Path skipped"]
```

When the agent's execution output contains file paths matching supported extensions, the interface automatically tries to resolve them — checking the absolute path, the current working directory, and the agent's data directory in order ([lines 2866–2875](biomni/agent/a1.py#L2866-L2875)). Images are rendered inline using `gr.Image()`, while PDFs are shown as clickable links.

Sources: [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L2683-L2687), [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L2841-L2895)

## Conversation History

The interface maintains conversation history across multiple turns. Internally, it keeps a copy of the full conversation in `self.main_history_copy` ([line 2652](biomni/agent/a1.py#L2652)). Each time you submit a new prompt, all previous messages are converted back into LangChain `HumanMessage` and `AIMessage` objects and passed to the agent, giving it full context of the ongoing dialogue ([lines 2688–2696](biomni/agent/a1.py#L2688-L2696)).

The `thread_id` parameter controls which LangGraph conversation thread is used (via `configurable: {"thread_id": thread_id}` at [line 2700](biomni/agent/a1.py#L2700)). If you restart the Python script and use the same `thread_id`, the agent's internal LangGraph memory (checkpointer) will retain prior context. To start a fresh conversation, use a different `thread_id` or re-instantiate the agent.

Sources: [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L2652), [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L2688-L2700)

## Security Considerations

**⚠️ Important:** The Gradio interface executes LLM-generated code with full system privileges — the same as running the agent programmatically. This means the agent can read files, execute shell commands, make network requests, and install packages on your machine.

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Arbitrary code execution | Run in a Docker container or VM; never on a machine with sensitive data |
| Network exposure with `server_name="0.0.0.0"` | Enable `require_verification=True` and use a firewall |
| Public `share=True` link | Treat as temporary; expires when the process stops |
| Access code `"Biomni2025"` is well-known | Change the code in [`available_access_codes`](biomni/agent/a1.py#L2655) before deploying publicly |

For production or shared environments, consider the [commercial mode](20-commercial-vs-academic-mode) configuration and always run inside an isolated sandbox.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L404-L407), [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L2654-L2655)

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Likely Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `ImportError: Gradio is not installed` | Gradio not in environment | `pip install "gradio>=5.0,<6.0"` |
| `AttributeError` on `ChatMessage` or other Gradio types | Gradio 6.x installed | `pip install "gradio>=5.0,<6.0" --force-reinstall` |
| Interface loads but agent never responds | Missing or invalid API key | Verify `.env` file or environment variables per [API Key Configuration](3-api-key-configuration) |
| "Executor is working on it" but nothing happens | Data lake download in progress | First run downloads ~11GB; see [Quick Start](2-quick-start) for `expected_data_lake_files=[]` option |
| Images not appearing in Executor panel | File path resolution failed | Ensure generated files are in the current working directory or the agent's data path |
| Timeout after long tasks | Default 600s timeout exceeded | Increase via `A1(timeout_seconds=1200)` or `default_config.timeout_seconds = 1200` |

## Complete Example

Here is a ready-to-run script that sets up the agent with all recommended settings and launches the interface with verification enabled:

```python
from biomni.config import default_config
from biomni.agent import A1

# Configure global defaults
default_config.llm = "claude-sonnet-4-20250514"
default_config.timeout_seconds = 1200

# Initialize agent
agent = A1(path='./data')

# Launch with security settings
agent.launch_gradio_demo(
    server_name="0.0.0.0",
    require_verification=True,
)
```

Access the interface at `http://localhost:7860`, enter the access code `Biomni2025`, and start asking biomedical questions or uploading data files for analysis.

# Latest Updates



Biomni has evolved rapidly since its initial open-source release in mid-2025. What started as a bioRxiv preprint has grown into a living ecosystem -- new tools, new reasoning models, wet-lab automation partnerships, and an increasingly active contributor base. This page tracks the most significant changes across recent release cycles and highlights what developers and researchers should pay attention to right now.
