# A1 Agent Core Class



The `A1` class is the central orchestrator of the Biomni system — a biomedical AI agent that combines large language model reasoning with interactive code execution, tool retrieval, and domain-specific knowledge. Instantiating an `A1` object bootstraps the entire agent pipeline: it resolves configuration, downloads required data, registers tools, loads know-how documents, and compiles a LangGraph state-machine workflow ready to accept user prompts. This page dissects the class architecture, its lifecycle, and its public API for developers who need to understand or extend the agent's behavior.

Sources: [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L1-L50)

## Architectural Overview

At the highest level, `A1` is a stateful agent built on **LangGraph's** `StateGraph` with an in-memory checkpoint saver. Each invocation follows a generate → execute → route loop until the LLM emits a `<solution>` tag, at which point the graph terminates. The class manages four distinct resource domains — tools, data lake files, software libraries, and know-how documents — and selectively injects them into the system prompt either at initialization (full-dump mode) or at query time (retrieval mode).

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "A1 Lifecycle"
        A["Constructor __init__"] --> B[configure]
        B --> C["Compiled StateGraph"]
        C --> D{"go / go_stream"}
        D --> E["_prepare_resources_for_retrieval"]
        E --> F["update_system_prompt_with_selected_resources"]
        F --> G["Execute generate → execute loop"]
        G --> H["Return log + final message"]
    end

    subgraph "Resource Management"
        T[add_tool] --> B
        D2[add_data] --> B
        S[add_software] --> B
        M[add_mcp] --> B
    end

    subgraph "Workflow Graph"
        G2["generate node"] -->|"next=execute"| X["execute node"]
        X -->|"always"| G2
        G2 -->|"next=end"| END2[END]
        G2 -->|"next=generate"| G2
        X -->|"self_critic mode"| SC["self_critic node"]
        SC -->|"generate"| G2
        SC -->|"end"| END2
    end

    D --> G2
```

Sources: [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L1289-L1650), [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L1759-L1830)

## AgentState and State Graph

The graph is parameterized by a lightweight `TypedDict` called `AgentState`, carrying only two fields:

| Field | Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `messages` | `list[BaseMessage]` | Full conversation history including system prompts, human inputs, AI responses, and execution observations |
| `next_step` | `str \| None` | Routing signal set by the `generate` node: `"generate"`, `"execute"`, or `"end"` |

The `generate` node invokes the LLM with the system prompt plus conversation history, parses the response for XML tags (`<execute>`, `<solution>`, thinking delimiters), and sets `next_step` accordingly. The `execute` node runs code extracted from `<execute>` blocks — dispatching to Python REPL, R, or Bash based on leading markers (`#!R`, `#!BASH`, `#!CLI`) — and appends an `<observation>` message. A built-in timeout (default 600s) prevents runaway executions.

Sources: [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L51-L54), [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L1380-L1490)

## Constructor and Configuration

The `__init__` method accepts nine optional parameters that layer on top of the global `BiomniConfig` defaults. Any parameter left as `None` falls back to `default_config`, which itself respects environment variables like `BIOMNI_LLM`, `BIOMNI_PATH`, `BIOMNI_COMMERCIAL_MODE`, and others.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | `str \| None` | `"./data"` | Root data directory; `biomni_data/` subfolders are created automatically |
| `llm` | `str \| None` | `"claude-sonnet-4-5"` | LLM model identifier |
| `source` | `SourceType \| None` | Auto-detected | Provider: `"OpenAI"`, `"Anthropic"`, `"Ollama"`, `"Gemini"`, `"Bedrock"`, `"Custom"`, etc. |
| `use_tool_retriever` | `bool \| None` | `True` | Enable retrieval-augmented tool/data selection at query time |
| `timeout_seconds` | `int \| None` | `600` | Maximum execution time per code block |
| `base_url` | `str \| None` | `None` | Custom model endpoint URL (for self-hosted models) |
| `api_key` | `str \| None` | `"EMPTY"` | API key for custom model serving |
| `commercial_mode` | `bool \| None` | `False` | If `True`, excludes non-commercial datasets and know-how documents |
| `expected_data_lake_files` | `list \| None` | All files from `data_lake_dict` | Pass empty list to skip S3 auto-download |

During initialization the constructor performs several critical side-effects: it creates the `biomni_data/benchmark` and `biomni_data/data_lake` directory structure, downloads missing files from the Biomni S3 bucket, initializes the `ToolRegistry` and `ToolRetriever` (when retrieval is enabled), loads all know-how documents via `KnowHowLoader`, and calls `configure()` to compile the initial workflow.

Sources: [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L57-L224), [config.py](biomni/config.py#L12-L51)

## Resource Extension API

One of the core design patterns in `A1` is its symmetric CRUD interface for three resource types: **tools**, **data**, and **software**. Each resource type follows the same four-method pattern — `add_*`, `get_custom_*`, `list_custom_*`, `remove_custom_*` — with internal storage in `_custom_tools`, `_custom_data`, and `_custom_software` dictionaries. Every `add_*` call triggers `self.configure()` to rebuild the system prompt and recompile the workflow graph, ensuring the LLM always sees an up-to-date environment description.

**Adding tools** is the most involved operation. The `add_tool(api)` method accepts a callable, inspects its source code, generates an API schema via `function_to_api_schema()`, registers it in both `tool_registry` and `module2api`, and injects the function into `builtins._biomni_custom_functions` so it is available during Python REPL execution. This dual-registration ensures custom tools work both as direct imports in code and as retrieval candidates.

**Adding data** via `add_data(data)` accepts a `dict` mapping file paths to descriptions, while `add_software(software)` maps software names to descriptions. Both merge into the agent's internal dictionaries (`data_lake_dict`, `library_content_dict`) so they appear in system prompt generation and retrieval.

Sources: [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L225-L348), [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L676-L870), [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L777-L870)

## System Prompt Generation

The `_generate_system_prompt` method is the largest single method in the class (~390 lines) and is responsible for assembling the full system prompt from four resource categories. It handles two distinct modes controlled by the `is_retrieval` flag:

- **Initial configuration** (`is_retrieval=False`): All tools, data lake items, software libraries, and know-how documents are included with generic introductory text like *"In your code, you will need to import the function location using the following dictionary..."*
- **Post-retrieval** (`is_retrieval=True`): Only the resources selected by the retriever are included, with targeted framing like *"Based on your query, I've identified the following most relevant functions..."*

Custom resources are always highlighted with emoji prefixes (🔧 for tools, 📊 for data, ⚙️ for software, 📚 for know-how) and placed in a dedicated "PRIORITY CUSTOM RESOURCES" section at the top of the prompt. Know-how documents receive special treatment: their full content (with metadata stripped) is embedded directly, and the prompt explicitly instructs the LLM not to waste a step "retrieving" them since they are already in context.

The base prompt defines the agent's behavioral contract: think first with a numbered plan using checkbox notation, then either execute code via `<execute>` tags or provide a final answer via `<solution>` tags. It supports Python (default), R (`#!R`), and Bash (`#!BASH` / `#!CLI`) execution environments.

Sources: [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L898-L1288), [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L1075-L1130)

## Execution Flow: go() and go_stream()

The primary entry points for running the agent are `go(prompt)` and `go_stream(prompt)`. Both follow the same internal sequence:

1. Reset `critic_count` and store the user task
2. If `use_tool_retriever` is enabled, call `_prepare_resources_for_retrieval(prompt)` to select relevant tools, data, libraries, and know-how documents, then call `update_system_prompt_with_selected_resources()` to regenerate the system prompt with only those resources
3. Create the initial `AgentState` with the human message
4. Stream through the compiled `StateGraph` with a recursion limit of 500
5. Collect and return the log

The `go()` method returns a tuple of `(log, final_message_content)` after the graph completes. The `go_stream()` method yields `{"output": pretty_printed_message}` dictionaries as a generator, enabling real-time progress monitoring.

> [!TIP]
> The `_prepare_resources_for_retrieval` method delegates to `ToolRetriever.prompt_based_retrieval()`, which uses the agent's own LLM to select resources — not a separate embedding model. This means retrieval quality is directly tied to the configured LLM's capability and the prompt's clarity.

Sources: [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L1646-L1790), [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L1759-L1830)

## Self-Critic and Test-Time Scaling

When `configure(self_critic=True, test_time_scale_round=N)` is called, the graph gains an additional `self_critic` node positioned between the generate node and the END state. Once the LLM produces a `<solution>`, instead of terminating immediately, the graph routes to `self_critic`, which asks the LLM to critique its own work against the original user task. This critique is injected as a `HumanMessage` and the generate node runs again, producing a potentially improved solution. The cycle repeats up to `test_time_scale_round` times before terminating.

Sources: [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L1560-L1645)

## Commercial Mode Filtering

When `commercial_mode=True`, the constructor imports environment descriptors from `biomni.env_desc_cm` (instead of `biomni.env_desc`), which contains only commercially-licensed datasets. Additionally, `_filter_know_how_for_commercial_mode()` scans all loaded know-how documents and removes any whose metadata includes markers like `"❌"`, `"Not Allowed"`, or `"Non-Commercial"` in the `commercial_use` field. This ensures compliance with license terms at every layer of the resource stack.

Sources: [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L876-L895), [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L137-L142)

## MCP Integration and Server Creation

The `A1` class provides two MCP-related capabilities. `add_mcp(config_path)` reads a YAML configuration file and dynamically creates synchronous wrapper functions for each tool discovered from external MCP servers via stdio transport. `create_mcp_server(tool_modules)` reverses the direction — it takes the agent's internal `module2api` tool registry and exposes those tools as an MCP server using `FastMCP`, enabling other MCP clients to consume Biomni's native tools.

Both methods bridge the gap between Biomni's internal tool system and the broader MCP ecosystem, making it possible to both consume external tools and serve internal tools through a standardized protocol.

Sources: [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L350-L588), [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L1995-L2060)

## Quick Reference: Key Methods

| Method | Purpose | Triggers Reconfigure? |
|---|---|---|
| `__init__(...)` | Full agent bootstrap | Yes (via `configure()`) |
| `configure(self_critic, test_time_scale_round)` | Rebuild system prompt and compile graph | N/A (is the reconfigure) |
| `go(prompt)` | Run agent synchronously, return log + answer | No |
| `go_stream(prompt)` | Run agent as generator, yield steps | No |
| `add_tool(api)` | Register a custom callable as a tool | Yes |
| `add_data(data)` | Register custom data lake files | Yes |
| `add_software(software)` | Register custom software libraries | Yes |
| `add_mcp(config_path)` | Load external MCP server tools | Yes |
| `create_mcp_server(tool_modules)` | Expose internal tools as MCP server | No |
| `result_formatting(output_class, task_intention)` | Extract structured output from conversation | No |
| `save_conversation_history(filepath)` | Export conversation as PDF/Markdown | No |

For details on how the ReAct-style generate-execute loop works under the hood — including tag parsing, error recovery, and the routing logic — see the [ReAct Reasoning Engine](10-react-reasoning-engine) page. To understand how the tool retriever selects resources at query time, continue to [Retrieval-Augmented Tool Selection](13-retrieval-augmented-tool-selection). For a broader view of how `A1` fits within the overall system architecture, refer back to the [Architecture Overview](8-architecture-overview).


# ReAct Reasoning Engine



The `react` class in [biomni/agent/react.py](biomni/agent/react.py) implements the foundational **Reasoning + Acting** loop that powers BioMni's earlier agent architecture. Built on LangGraph's `StateGraph`, it provides a two-node cyclic graph where the LLM reasons about tool calls and a dedicated tool-execution node materializes those decisions — repeating until the model produces a final answer without further tool calls. While the newer [A1 Agent Core Class](9-a1-agent-core-class) supersedes this engine in production, the `react` class remains valuable for understanding the base reasoning loop, for lightweight deployments, and as a reference implementation for custom agent wiring.

## Core Architecture: Two-Node LangGraph Cycle

The entire reasoning engine reduces to a deterministic two-node directed cycle. At initialization the constructor discovers every registered tool via `read_module2api()`, converts each API schema into a LangChain `StructuredTool` through `api_schema_to_langchain_tool`, wraps each tool with a multiprocessing-based timeout, and stores the resulting tool list ([react.py#L64-L71](biomni/agent/react.py#L64-L71)). The graph itself is constructed inside [`_create_custom_react_agent`](biomni/agent/react.py#L268-L345), which follows the canonical ReAct pattern with three components:

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    direction LR

    [*] --> agent: User prompt
    
    state agent {
        [*] --> llm_inference
        llm_inference --> decision: "tool_calls present?"
        decision --> end_state: "No → return final response"
        decision --> continue_state: "Yes → return tool call"
    }
    
    state tools {
        [*] --> execute_calls
        execute_calls --> collect_results
        collect_results --> [*]: "ToolMessages appended"
    }

    agent --> tools: continue
    tools --> agent: ToolMessages
    end_state --> [*]
```

The **agent node** ([L277-L282](biomni/agent/react.py#L277-L282)) prepends the system prompt as a `SystemMessage`, invokes the LLM with all accumulated messages, and returns the model's response — which either contains `tool_calls` (triggering a loop continuation) or a plain text response (ending the loop). The **tools node** ([L285-L307](biomni/agent/react.py#L285-L307)) iterates over every tool call in the last AI message, looks up the tool by name in a dictionary, invokes it with the provided arguments, and serializes the result into a `ToolMessage`. Errors are caught gracefully and returned as error-bearing `ToolMessage` objects, preventing a single tool failure from crashing the entire loop. The **conditional edge** [`should_continue`](biomni/agent/react.py#L310-L319) inspects the last message: if `tool_calls` is empty or absent it routes to `END`, otherwise to the `tools` node. The graph is compiled with a recursion limit of 50 iterations ([L438](biomni/agent/react.py#L438)).

| Component | Location | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `call_model` | [L277-L282](biomni/agent/react.py#L277-L282) | Prepend system prompt, invoke LLM, return response |
| `tool_node` | [L285-L307](biomni/agent/react.py#L285-L307) | Execute tool calls, serialize results to `ToolMessage` |
| `should_continue` | [L310-L319](biomni/agent/react.py#L310-L319) | Route to `END` or `tools` based on presence of `tool_calls` |
| `StateGraph` | [L322-L345](biomni/agent/react.py#L322-L345) | Wire nodes, edges, and compile the runnable graph |

Sources: [react.py](biomni/agent/react.py#L268-L345)

## Tool Timeout Isolation

Every tool function is wrapped in a **multiprocessing-based timeout** during initialization via [`_add_timeout_to_tools`](biomni/agent/react.py#L90-L152). The factory function `create_timed_func` spawns each tool invocation in an isolated `Process`, communicates results through a `multiprocessing.Queue`, and enforces a configurable timeout (default 600 seconds from [`BiomniConfig`](biomni/config.py#L33)). If the process exceeds the timeout, it is first asked to terminate gracefully, then killed with `SIGKILL` if unresponsive. The timeout mechanism is crucial because biomedical tools — sequence BLASTs, PDB queries, image processing — can hang unpredictably on external services. The `react` class wraps tools at initialization ([L86](biomni/agent/react.py#L86)), and newly added tools via [`add_tool`](biomni/agent/react.py#L154-L164) are automatically wrapped before being appended to the tool list.

> [!TIP]
> The timeout wrapper uses `multiprocessing.Process` rather than `threading.Timer` because it enables true OS-level process isolation via `SIGKILL` — essential when a tool spawns subprocesses or opens network connections that would survive thread cancellation.

Sources: [react.py](biomni/agent/react.py#L90-L152), [config.py](biomni/config.py#L33)

## Configuration Modes: Plan, Reflect, and Resource Access

The [`configure`](biomni/agent/react.py#L166-L266) method accepts five boolean flags that compose the system prompt and determine which tools and resources the agent can access. These flags are mutually combinable, producing four distinct prompt strategies:

| `plan` | `reflect` | Prompt Strategy | Behavior |
|---|---|---|---|
| `False` | `False` | **Direct** ([L193-L194](biomni/agent/react.py#L193-L194)) | Straightforward tool-use without meta-reasoning |
| `True` | `False` | **Plan** ([L196-L202](biomni/agent/react.py#L196-L202)) | Agent maintains a Research Plan tracking high-level strategy, completed steps, and short conclusions |
| `False` | `True` | **Reflect** ([L203-L206](biomni/agent/react.py#L203-L206)) | After each tool use the agent reflects: what does the observation mean, what caused errors, how to debug |
| `True` | `True` | **Plan + Reflect** ([L208-L216](biomni/agent/react.py#L208-L216)) | Full meta-cognitive loop with research plan maintenance and post-action reflection, plus explicit `write_python_code` and `run_python_repl` tool instructions for data-heavy tasks |

The `data_lake` flag ([L218-L234](biomni/agent/react.py#L218-L234)) appends descriptions of all files found in `{path}/data_lake/` to the system prompt, giving the agent awareness of available datasets. The `library_access` flag ([L236-L250](biomni/agent/react.py#L236-L250)) appends available software library descriptions from `library_content_dict`. Both are purely prompt-level augmentations — they instruct the agent to use `run_python_repl` for data access but do not inject new tools into the graph. There is also a special `react_code_search` mode ([L178-L189](biomni/agent/react.py#L178-L189)) that restricts the tool set to only `run_python_repl` and `search_google`, stripping away the full biomedical toolkit for pure code+search tasks.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    C[configure call] --> R{react_code_search?}
    R -->|Yes| CS[Tools: run_python_repl + search_google]
    R -->|No| F{Full toolkit}
    
    F --> P{plan?}
    F --> RF{reflect?}
    
    P -->|Yes| PM[Plan prompt: research plan tracking]
    P -->|No| NM[Minimal prompt: helpful biologist]
    
    RF -->|Yes| RM[+ Reflection after each tool use]
    RF -->|No| NOP[No reflection step]
    
    PM --> DL{data_lake?}
    NM --> DL
    DL -->|Yes| DLA[+ Data lake descriptions in prompt]
    DL -->|No| LA{library_access?}
    DLA --> LA
    LA -->|Yes| LIB[+ Library descriptions in prompt]
    LA -->|No| BUILD[Build _create_custom_react_agent]
    LIB --> BUILD
    CS --> BUILD
    
    BUILD --> APP[Compiled LangGraph app ready]
```

Sources: [react.py](biomni/agent/react.py#L166-L266)

## Retrieval-Augmented Tool Selection

When `use_tool_retriever` is `True` (the default per [`BiomniConfig`](biomni/config.py#L40)), the agent does not blindly pass all registered tools to the LLM. Instead, at execution time inside [`go`](biomni/agent/react.py#L347-L445), it performs a **prompt-based retrieval** step that narrows the tool set to a query-relevant subset before constructing the LangGraph. This is the same retrieval mechanism documented in [Retrieval-Augmented Tool Selection](13-retrieval-augmented-tool-selection), integrated here as an optional pre-execution phase.

The retrieval process works as follows:

1. **Resource assembly** ([L375-L379](biomni/agent/react.py#L375-L379)): All registered tools, data lake items (with descriptions from `data_lake_dict`), and library entries (from `library_content_dict`) are collected into a unified resources dictionary.

2. **Prompt-based selection** ([L382](biomni/agent/react.py#L382)): The [`ToolRetriever.prompt_based_retrieval`](biomni/model/retriever.py#L14-L132) method constructs a selection prompt that lists all available resources with indices and asks the LLM to output index lists for each category. The retriever's guidelines ([retriever.py#L77-L87](biomni/model/retriever.py#L77-L87)) are deliberately generous — it prefers inclusion over exclusion, particularly for database tools and molecular biology tools.

3. **Graph reconstruction** ([L414-L435](biomni/agent/react.py#L414-L435)): Selected tool names are matched back to their LangChain tool objects. The `run_python_repl` tool is always force-included if not already selected ([L428-L431](biomni/agent/react.py#L428-L431)), as it serves as the agent's fallback code execution environment. The LangGraph is then **recompiled** with only the retrieved tool subset via `_create_custom_react_agent`.

This approach dramatically reduces the token overhead of tool schemas in the LLM context window, which is critical when the full registry contains hundreds of biomedical tools across genomics, proteomics, imaging, and other domains.

Sources: [react.py](biomni/agent/react.py#L347-L445), [retriever.py](biomni/model/retriever.py#L14-L132)

## Execution Flow: The `go` Method

The [`go`](biomni/agent/react.py#L347-L445) method is the single entry point for executing a query. It accepts a natural-language prompt and returns a tuple of `(log, final_response)`. The execution proceeds in three phases:

**Phase 1 — Retrieval (conditional).** If `use_tool_retriever` is enabled, the retrieval phase described above runs, narrowing the tool set and recompiling the graph.

**Phase 2 — Streaming execution.** The compiled LangGraph app is invoked with `stream_mode="values"` ([L441](biomni/agent/react.py#L441)), yielding the full message state after each graph step. This means every intermediate step — LLM reasoning, tool calls, tool results — is available in real time through the stream. Each yielded message is processed through `pretty_print` for console output and appended to `self.log`.

**Phase 3 — Result extraction.** After the stream completes, the final message content is returned as the response string. The full conversation log is stored in `self.log` for downstream processing.

> [!TIP]
> The `recursion_limit` is hardcoded to 50 at [L438](biomni/agent/react.py#L438). Each tool invocation counts as one recursion step. For complex multi-step biological analyses, this limit can be reached — if you see `GraphRecursionError`, consider raising this value or simplifying the task.

Sources: [react.py](biomni/agent/react.py#L347-L445)

## Result Formatting

The [`result_formatting`](biomni/agent/react.py#L447-L465) method provides structured output extraction from the conversation log. It invokes the same LLM as a "evaluateGPT" role, passing the full conversation history along with a `task_intention` string that describes the expected output schema. The LLM is invoked with `with_structured_output(output_class)`, which forces it to produce a response conforming to the provided Pydantic model or TypedDict. This enables downstream evaluation pipelines to extract structured answers from the agent's free-form reasoning chain — a pattern used extensively in [Biomni-Eval1 Benchmark Results](7-biomni-eval1-benchmark-results).

Sources: [react.py](biomni/agent/react.py#L447-L465)

## Relationship to the A1 Agent

The `react` class is the **predecessor** to the production [`A1`](biomni/agent/a1.py#L56) agent. While `react` uses a minimal two-node `StateGraph` with `Annotated[Sequence[BaseMessage], add_messages]` state ([react.py#L31-L35](biomni/agent/react.py#L31-L35)), A1 introduces a richer state model with `next_step` routing ([a1.py#L51-L53](biomni/agent/a1.py#L51-L53)), memory checkpointing via `MemorySaver`, multi-step planning with `START` nodes, know-how document integration, MCP server support, conversation persistence, and a Gradio web interface. The `react` class is **not exported** from [`biomni/agent/__init__.py`](biomni/agent/__init__.py) — only `A1` is — but `react` can be imported directly from `biomni.agent.react` for lightweight use cases.

| Feature | `react` class | `A1` class |
|---|---|---|
| State model | `AgentState` with `messages` only | `AgentState` with `messages` + `next_step` |
| Graph complexity | 2-node cycle | Multi-node with `START`, conditional routing |
| Memory persistence | None | `MemorySaver` checkpointing |
| Know-how integration | No | Yes, via `KnowHowLoader` |
| Tool retrieval | Built-in, per-execution | Built-in, with richer resource types |
| MCP support | No | Yes |
| Conversation export | No | Markdown + PDF export |
| Gradio UI | No | Yes, built-in |
| Self-critic / test-time scaling | No | Yes ([Self-Critic and Test-Time Scaling](11-self-critic-and-test-time-scaling)) |

Sources: [react.py#L31-L35](biomni/agent/react.py#L31-L35), [a1.py#L51-L53](biomni/agent/a1.py#L51-L53), [__init__.py](biomni/agent/__init__.py)

## Minimal Usage Example

For developers who want a lightweight agent without the full A1 feature set, the `react` class provides a straightforward API:

```python
from biomni.agent.react import react

# Initialize with defaults (Claude Sonnet 4.5, tool retriever enabled)
agent = react()

# Configure with planning mode and data lake access
agent.configure(
    plan=True,
    reflect=True,
    data_lake=True,
    library_access=False,
)

# Execute a query
log, response = agent.go(
    "Design a CRISPR guide RNA targeting the BRCA1 gene exon 5"
)
print(response)
```

The `configure` call must precede `go` — attempting to call `go` before `configure` will raise an error because `self.app` (the compiled graph) has not been created.

## Continuing the Architecture Tour

The ReAct reasoning engine defines the base reasoning loop that underpins BioMni's agent system. To understand the production agent that builds upon this foundation — with memory, self-criticism, know-how integration, and MCP support — proceed to [A1 Agent Core Class](9-a1-agent-core-class). For the meta-cognitive enhancements layered on top of the base loop, see [Self-Critic and Test-Time Scaling](11-self-critic-and-test-time-scaling). To understand how tools are discovered, registered, and filtered before being passed into this engine, explore [Tool Registry and Discovery](12-tool-registry-and-discovery) and [Retrieval-Augmented Tool Selection](13-retrieval-augmented-tool-selection).

# Self-Critic and Test-Time Scaling



Biomni's agent framework incorporates two complementary inference-time strategies—**self-criticism** and **test-time scaling**—that transform a single-pass generation into an iterative refinement loop. Rather than accepting the first solution produced by the LLM, these mechanisms force the agent to re-examine its own reasoning, identify deficiencies, and produce improved answers. Both are controlled through the `A1.configure()` method and implemented as a dedicated node within the LangGraph state machine.

## Architectural Motivation: Why Self-Criticism?

The default A1 agent operates in a single-attempt mode: the generate node reasons and emits either an `<execute>` block (for tool interaction) or a `<solution>` block (for a final answer), and once a solution is emitted, the workflow terminates. For complex biomedical tasks—multi-step experimental design, cross-database analysis, or protocol generation—a single pass often yields incomplete or suboptimal results. Self-criticism addresses this by inserting an adversarial review step between solution emission and final termination, creating a feedback loop that mimics iterative peer review.

Sources: [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L1579-L1604)

## The Self-Critic Node: Internal Adversarial Feedback

The `execute_self_critic` function is the computational core of this strategy. When activated, it intercepts the workflow after the agent produces its first `<solution>` response. Instead of terminating, the state machine routes to this node, which performs three operations:

1. **Task reminder injection**: The node prepends the original user task (`self.user_task`) into a feedback prompt, ensuring the critic never loses sight of the ground-truth objective.
2. **Harsh criticism generation**: The agent's own LLM is invoked with the full conversation history plus a directive to "critic harshly" on what could be improved, what is missing, and what remains to solve the task. The feedback is explicitly constrained—no questions allowed, only constructive critique.
3. **State transition**: The criticism is injected as a synthetic `HumanMessage` into the message list, framed as "this is not enough to solve the task," and the workflow routes back to the `generate` node for another attempt.

The critical design insight is that the same LLM serves dual roles: as both the **solver** and the **critic**. This eliminates the need for a separate critic model while leveraging the model's own capacity for self-evaluation. The `critic_count` instance variable on the `A1` class tracks how many criticism cycles have elapsed ([a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L1766-L1767)).

Sources: [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L1579-L1604), [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L1766-L1767)

## Test-Time Scaling: Budget-Controlled Iteration

Test-time scaling in Biomni is implemented as a bounded repetition mechanism controlled by the `test_time_scale_round` parameter. This integer determines the maximum number of self-criticism cycles the agent will perform before being forced to terminate. The relationship between the two mechanisms is direct: self-criticism provides the *logic* of improvement, while test-time scaling provides the *budget* that governs how many improvement iterations are permitted.

When `execute_self_critic` is called, it checks `self.critic_count < test_time_scale_round`. If the budget is exhausted, the node routes directly to `"end"` rather than back to `"generate"`. This creates a predictable compute-time/compute-quality tradeoff that scales linearly with the round count.

Sources: [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L1289-L1296), [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L1579-L1604)

## State Machine Topology

The following diagram contrasts the two workflow configurations. The left graph shows standard (non-critic) execution, where a `<solution>` tag immediately terminates. The right graph shows the self-critic variant, where solution emission routes through the critic node before either looping back or terminating.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph Standard Mode
        direction TB
        S1[START] --> G1[generate]
        G1 -->|"&lt;execute&gt;"| E1[execute]
        G1 -->|"&lt;solution&gt;"| END1[END]
        G1 -->|thinking only| G1
        E1 --> G1
    end

    subgraph Self-Critic Mode
        direction TB
        S2[START] --> G2[generate]
        G2 -->|"&lt;execute&gt;"| E2[execute]
        G2 -->|"&lt;solution&gt;"| SC[self_critic]
        G2 -->|thinking only| G2
        E2 --> G2
        SC -->|critic_count &lt; budget| G2
        SC -->|critic_count ≥ budget| END2[END]
    end
```

The routing functions differ between modes. Standard mode uses `routing_function` which maps `"end"` directly to the terminal `END` node ([a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L1555-L1566)). Self-critic mode uses `routing_function` for the generate node but maps `"end"` to the `self_critic` node ([a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L1613-L1624)), then uses `routing_function_self_critic` which only recognizes `"generate"` and `"end"`—deliberately excluding `"execute"` since the critic should not trigger code execution directly ([a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L1568-L1577)).

Sources: [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L1606-L1641)

## System Prompt Modifications for Self-Critic Mode

When `self_critic=True` is passed to `_generate_system_prompt`, the system prompt receives an additional instruction block that prepares the agent for iterative refinement. This instruction tells the agent it "may or may not receive feedback from human" and to "address the feedbacks by following the same procedure of multiple rounds of thinking, execution, and then coming up with a new solution" ([a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L1146-L1149)). This is critical because the synthetic criticism messages injected by `execute_self_critic` appear as `HumanMessage` instances—the agent must be primed to treat them as legitimate feedback rather than unexpected interruptions.

Sources: [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L1146-L1149)

## Activation and Configuration

Both mechanisms are activated through the `configure()` method on the `A1` class. Since `configure()` is called automatically during `__init__` ([a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L223)), enabling self-criticism requires a two-step pattern: instantiate the agent, then re-configure.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `self_critic` | `bool` | `False` | Enables the self-critic review node in the workflow graph |
| `test_time_scale_round` | `int` | `0` | Maximum number of self-criticism iterations before forced termination |

**Usage pattern:**

```python
from biomni.agent import A1

agent = A1(llm="claude-sonnet-4-5")
agent.configure(self_critic=True, test_time_scale_round=3)
log, answer = agent.go("Design a CRISPR screening experiment...")
```

> [!TIP]
> The `critic_count` and `user_task` attributes are initialized at the start of each `go()` or `go_stream()` call ([a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L1766-L1767)), not during `configure()`. This means the same agent instance can safely handle multiple sequential queries without state leakage between critic cycles.

Sources: [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L1289-L1296), [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L1759-L1789)

## Execution Lifecycle During Self-Critic Iterations

Each full iteration through the self-critic loop follows a predictable message sequence in the conversation state. Understanding this pattern is essential for debugging and for consuming streamed outputs:

1. **Generate phase**: The LLM receives the accumulated message history (including prior criticisms) and produces either a new `<execute>` block or a revised `<solution>` block.
2. **Execute phase** (if applicable): Tool invocations are run through the Python/R/Bash REPL with timeout enforcement. Results are appended as `<observation>` messages.
3. **Solution emission**: When the LLM finally emits a `<solution>`, the `routing_function` maps `"end"` to the `self_critic` node (in critic mode).
4. **Critic invocation**: The `execute_self_critic` node calls the LLM with the full history plus the criticism prompt, producing a feedback string.
5. **Feedback injection**: The feedback is wrapped in a synthetic `HumanMessage`: "Wait... this is not enough to solve the task. Here are some feedbacks for improvement:\n{feedback}" ([a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L1594-L1598)).
6. **Budget check**: If `critic_count` has reached `test_time_scale_round`, the workflow terminates; otherwise, control returns to the generate phase.

The `recursion_limit` in the stream config is set to 500 ([a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L1774)), providing ample headroom for multi-round critic loops even on complex tasks with many intermediate execution steps.

Sources: [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L1774), [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L1594-L1598)

## Interaction with Tool Retrieval

Self-criticism operates orthogonally to the tool retrieval system. When `use_tool_retriever=True` (the default in [config.py](biomni/config.py#L40)), the `go()` method first performs prompt-based resource retrieval before entering the workflow ([a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L1769-L1771)). This means the selected tool set is determined once at invocation time and remains fixed across all critic iterations. The critic reviews the agent's *use* of those tools, not the tool selection itself. This separation ensures that test-time scaling does not compound retrieval costs across iterations.

Sources: [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L1769-L1771), [config.py](biomni/config.py#L40)

## Streaming Compatibility

The `go_stream()` method supports self-critic and test-time scaling identically to `go()`. The `critic_count` and `user_task` are reset at stream initialization ([a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L1803-L1804)), and each state update—including critic feedback messages—is yielded as part of the generator output. This enables real-time UI rendering of the critique-and-revise cycle in the Gradio interface, though the current Gradio demo does not expose self-critic as a user-togglable option—it always uses whatever configuration the agent was initialized with.

Sources: [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L1791-L1828)

## Cost and Latency Considerations

Each self-critic iteration adds a full LLM invocation (the criticism generation) plus whatever subsequent generate-execute cycles the agent performs in response. The total compute cost scales approximately as `base_cost × (1 + N × k)` where `N` is `test_time_scale_round` and `k` is the average number of generate-execute cycles per revision attempt. There is no mechanism for early stopping based on solution quality—all configured rounds are executed.

> [!TIP]
> For production deployments where latency matters, start with `test_time_scale_round=1` (single revision pass) and increase only if evaluation metrics justify the additional compute. The `BiomniEval1` benchmark ([biomni_eval1.py](biomni/eval/biomni_eval1.py)) can be used to quantify the accuracy lift from additional scaling rounds.

## Relationship to Other Agent Modes

The self-critic mechanism is exclusive to the A1 agent class. The `react` agent ([react.py](biomni/agent/react.py)) implements its own reflection capability via the `reflect` parameter in `configure()` ([react.py](biomni/agent/react.py#L166-L173)), which is a structurally different approach using LangGraph's built-in reflection patterns. The `qa_llm` agent ([qa_llm.py](biomni/agent/qa_llm.py)) is a single-shot Q&A wrapper with no iteration capability. For a full architectural comparison of these agent modes, see [ReAct Reasoning Engine](10-react-reasoning-engine) and [A1 Agent Core Class](9-a1-agent-core-class).


# Tool Registry and Discovery



The Biomni platform manages hundreds of bioinformatics tools across 22 life-science domains through a centralized registry and intelligent retrieval pipeline. Understanding how tools are authored, registered, discovered, and selected at runtime is essential for extending the system or diagnosing agent behavior. This page traces the full lifecycle — from static tool description files through registry construction to prompt-based tool retrieval — and explains the data contracts that bind each stage together.

## The Tool Lifecycle: From Description to Retrieval

Biomni's tool system follows a three-phase pipeline: **authoring**, **registration**, and **retrieval**. Tool descriptions live as Python data structures in domain-organized modules; at startup they are loaded into a `ToolRegistry` that assigns stable integer IDs and builds an index dataframe; during agent inference a `ToolRetriever` consults an LLM to select the most relevant subset for the user's query. Each phase has a clear data contract, and the boundaries between them are deliberately simple — raw dictionaries flow from description to registry, and registry entries flow to the retriever.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph Authoring
        TD["tool_description/*.py<br/>22 domain modules"]
        FD["function_to_api_schema()<br/>LLM-generated schema"]
    end

    subgraph Registration
        R2API["read_module2api()"]
        TR["ToolRegistry"]
        DDF["document_df<br/>(pandas DataFrame)"]
    end

    subgraph Retrieval
        TRL["ToolRetriever"]
        SEL["Selected subset<br/>for system prompt"]
    end

    TD -->|"import module.description"| R2API
    FD -->|"A1.add_tool(api)"| TR
    R2API -->|"dict of lists"| TR
    TR -->|"index rebuild"| DDF
    DDF -->|"formatted prompt"| TRL
    TRL -->|"indices → resources"| SEL
```

The following sections examine each phase in detail, with exact source references.

## Tool Description Format

Every tool in Biomni is described by a dictionary conforming to a lightweight schema enforced by `ToolRegistry.validate_tool()`. The three mandatory keys are `name`, `description`, and `required_parameters`; an `optional_parameters` key is present in the vast majority of tools but is not formally required by validation logic.

| Key | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `str` | ✅ | Unique function name used as the dispatch identifier |
| `description` | `str` | ✅ | Natural-language summary used by both the LLM agent and the retriever |
| `required_parameters` | `list[dict]` | ✅ | Parameters without defaults; each entry has `name`, `type`, `description`, `default` |
| `optional_parameters` | `list[dict]` | ❌ | Parameters with defaults; same sub-key structure as required |

Each parameter entry within the lists carries four sub-keys: `name` (string), `type` (string, e.g. `"str"`, `"int"`, `"List[str]"`), `description` (string), and `default` (value or `None`). This structure is consistent across all 22 domain modules in `biomni/tool/tool_description/`. For example, the `query_uniprot` tool in the database module demonstrates the canonical shape:

```python
{
    "description": "Query the UniProt REST API using either natural language or a direct endpoint.",
    "name": "query_uniprot",
    "optional_parameters": [
        {"default": None, "description": "Full or partial UniProt API endpoint URL…", "name": "endpoint", "type": "str"},
        {"default": 5, "description": "Maximum number of results to return", "name": "max_results", "type": "int"},
    ],
    "required_parameters": [
        {"default": None, "description": "Natural language query about proteins…", "name": "prompt", "type": "str"}
    ],
}
```

Sources: [tool_description/database.py](/biomni/tool/tool_description/database.py#L1-L22), [tool_registry.py](/biomni/tool/tool_registry.py#L32-L34)

## Static Description Modules

Tool descriptions are organized as Python source files under `biomni/tool/tool_description/`, with one file per scientific domain. Each module exports a single list variable named `description` containing all tool dictionaries for that domain. The `read_module2api()` function in `biomni/utils.py` orchestrates loading by iterating over a hardcoded list of 22 field names, importing the corresponding `biomni.tool.tool_description.<field>` module, and mapping the module's import path to its `description` list.

The 22 registered domains and their module keys are:

| Domain | Module Key | Description Scope |
|---|---|---|
| Literature | `literature` | PubMed search, paper retrieval |
| Biochemistry | `biochemistry` | Enzyme kinetics, metabolic pathways |
| Bioimaging | `bioimaging` | Microscopy image analysis |
| Bioengineering | `bioengineering` | Tissue engineering, biomaterials |
| Biophysics | `biophysics` | Molecular dynamics, structural modeling |
| Glycoengineering | `glycoengineering` | Glycan design and analysis |
| Cancer Biology | `cancer_biology` | Oncology analysis tools |
| Cell Biology | `cell_biology` | Cell culture, flow cytometry |
| Molecular Biology | `molecular_biology` | PCR, cloning, sequence manipulation |
| Genetics | `genetics` | Variant calling, genotype analysis |
| Genomics | `genomics` | scRNA-seq annotation, genomic pipelines |
| Immunology | `immunology` | Immune repertoire, antibody analysis |
| Microbiology | `microbiology` | Pathogen identification, antimicrobial |
| Pathology | `pathology` | Histopathology, diagnostic markers |
| Pharmacology | `pharmacology` | Drug interaction, dose-response |
| Physiology | `physiology` | Physiological modeling |
| Synthetic Biology | `synthetic_biology` | Circuit design, genetic constructs |
| Systems Biology | `systems_biology` | Network analysis, pathway modeling |
| Support Tools | `support_tools` | REPL execution, code reading, data download |
| Database | `database` | 30+ external database APIs |
| Lab Automation | `lab_automation` | Robotic protocols, PyLabRobot |
| Protocols | `protocols` | Wet-lab protocol generation |

The resulting `module2api` dictionary uses the fully-qualified module path (e.g. `"biomni.tool.database"`) as keys, pointing to the list of tool dictionaries. This two-level structure — module then tool list — is preserved throughout the registry and system prompt generation pipeline.

Sources: [utils.py](/biomni/utils.py#L845-L876)

## Database Schema Serialization

In addition to the Python description files, 34 pre-serialized database schemas are stored as pickle files under `biomni/tool/schema_db/`. These correspond to the `database` domain's tool descriptions and cover major bioinformatics databases: UniProt, PDB, KEGG, ChEMBL, ClinVar, dbSNP, gnomAD, Reactome, Ensembl, STRING, Open Targets, GWAS Catalog, JASPAR, ENCODE, cBioPortal, and many others. These `.pkl` files are consumed by database tool implementations to provide structured API metadata without runtime generation overhead.

Sources: [schema_db/](/biomni/tool/schema_db/)

## ToolRegistry Class

The `ToolRegistry` class in `biomni/tool/tool_registry.py` is the central in-memory index for all tools. It is constructed with a `module2api` dictionary and performs three operations at initialization: iterates over every module's tool list, validates and registers each tool with an auto-incrementing integer ID, and builds a pandas DataFrame mapping `docid` to full tool dictionaries for downstream retrieval.

### Construction and Initialization

```python
registry = ToolRegistry(module2api)
# Internally: for each module's tool list → register_tool(tool) → assign ID
# Then: builds document_df with columns ["docid", "document_content"]
```

The constructor's nested loop flattens the module-keyed dictionary into a single linear list, giving each tool a globally unique integer ID starting from zero. This ID is the primary key used by the retriever to reference tools by index.

Sources: [tool_registry.py](/biomni/tool/tool_registry.py#L7-L18)

### CRUD Operations

The registry exposes a symmetric set of lookup and mutation methods, all operating on the internal `self.tools` list:

| Method | Signature | Returns | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `register_tool` | `(tool: dict) → None` | — | Validates, assigns `id`, appends; raises `ValueError` on invalid format |
| `validate_tool` | `(tool: dict) → bool` | `bool` | Checks for `name`, `description`, `required_parameters` keys |
| `get_tool_by_name` | `(name: str) → dict \| None` | Tool dict or `None` | Linear scan by `name` field |
| `get_tool_by_id` | `(tool_id: int) → dict \| None` | Tool dict or `None` | Linear scan by `id` field |
| `get_id_by_name` | `(name: str) → int \| None` | Integer ID or `None` | Inverse lookup |
| `get_name_by_id` | `(tool_id: int) → str \| None` | Tool name or `None` | Inverse lookup |
| `list_tools` | `() → list[dict]` | `[{"name", "id"}, …]` | Summary list without full schemas |
| `remove_tool_by_id` | `(tool_id: int) → bool` | Success flag | Filters out tool; does not re-index remaining IDs |
| `remove_tool_by_name` | `(name: str) → bool` | Success flag | Same as above by name |
| `save_registry` | `(filename: str) → None` | — | Pickles entire registry to disk |
| `load_registry` | `(filename: str) → ToolRegistry` | Registry instance | Static method; unpickles from disk |

The lookup methods use linear scans, which is acceptable given the registry size (typically a few hundred tools). The `remove` methods filter the list in-place but do not compact IDs, meaning removed IDs create gaps — a design choice that preserves referential stability if any external system has cached an ID.

Sources: [tool_registry.py](/biomni/tool/tool_registry.py#L24-L88)

### Persistence

The registry supports serialization via Python's `pickle` module through `save_registry()` and `load_registry()`. This enables snapshotting the full registry state (including all tool dictionaries, the ID counter, and the document DataFrame) for caching or transfer. The `load_registry` method is annotated as `@staticmethod`, so it does not require an existing instance.

Sources: [tool_registry.py](/biomni/tool/tool_registry.py#L79-L89)

## Connection to the A1 Agent

The `ToolRegistry` is instantiated inside `A1.__init__()` but only when the `use_tool_retriever` flag is `True` (it defaults to the `default_config.use_tool_retriever` value). The `module2api` dictionary — loaded via `read_module2api()` — is passed directly to the `ToolRegistry` constructor, and a `ToolRetriever` instance is created alongside it.

The `module2api` dictionary is always loaded regardless of the retriever flag, because it is also used to build the system prompt when retrieval is disabled (tools are listed directly in the prompt text via `textify_api_dict()`). When retrieval is enabled, the registry and retriever take over the responsibility of narrowing the tool set before system prompt construction.

Sources: [a1.py](/biomni/agent/a1.py#L195-L213)

## Runtime Tool Registration

Biomni supports adding tools at runtime via `A1.add_tool(api)`, which accepts any callable Python function and performs a multi-step registration pipeline:

1. **Schema generation** — The function's source code is extracted via `inspect.getsource()` and passed to `function_to_api_schema()` along with the agent's LLM. This utility uses a structured-output prompt to convert raw Python code into the canonical tool dictionary format, retrying up to 7 times on parse failures.
2. **Schema validation and enrichment** — Missing `name`, `description`, or `required_parameters` fields are backfilled. The originating module name is attached under a `module` key.
3. **Registry update** — If a `tool_registry` exists, the schema is registered via `ToolRegistry.register_tool()`. The registry's `document_df` is then fully rebuilt to include the new entry.
4. **Module map update** — The tool is appended to `module2api[module_name]` (or updates an existing entry if the name already exists).
5. **Execution environment injection** — The function is stored in `builtins._biomni_custom_functions` and `self._custom_functions`, making it available both for direct REPL execution and for tool-call parsing.

After registration, `A1.configure()` is called to rebuild the agent's system prompt and workflow graph, ensuring the new tool is visible to the LLM on subsequent turns.

> [!TIP]
> When adding tools at runtime, `add_tool()` calls `self.configure()` internally, which fully rebuilds the LangGraph workflow. Avoid adding tools inside a loop or during an active agent turn — batch all additions before calling `go()`.

Sources: [a1.py](/biomni/agent/a1.py#L225-L348), [utils.py](/biomni/utils.py#L251-L289)

## The Retrieval Gateway

When `use_tool_retriever` is enabled, the `ToolRetriever` class in `biomni/model/retriever.py` acts as the gateway between the full registry and the agent's system prompt. Rather than embedding-based similarity search, Biomni uses a **prompt-based retrieval** strategy: the retriever formats all available tools, data lake items, software libraries, and know-how documents into a structured prompt, asks the LLM to select relevant indices, and returns a filtered subset.

The retriever's `prompt_based_retrieval()` method receives a `resources` dictionary with four optional keys (`tools`, `data_lake`, `libraries`, `know_how`), each containing a list. It formats each list as an indexed enumeration (e.g., `"0. query_uniprot: Query the UniProt REST API…"`) and instructs the LLM to return index lists for each category. The response is parsed via regex patterns matching `TOOLS: [0, 3, 5]`, `DATA_LAKE: [1, 2]`, etc.

The retrieval prompt includes domain-specific heuristics — it instructs the LLM to "be generous," prioritize database tools, always include literature search tools, and include molecular biology tools for wet-lab sequence queries. This bias toward inclusion reduces the risk of missing relevant tools at the cost of slightly larger system prompts.

Sources: [retriever.py](/biomni/model/retriever.py#L14-L132)

## System Prompt Integration

Whether retrieval is enabled or not, the final tool set is rendered into the agent's system prompt. The `textify_api_dict()` utility in `biomni/utils.py` converts the module-keyed tool dictionary into a structured text format with section headers, method names, descriptions, and parameter tables. Each tool becomes a block that the LLM reads as part of its available API surface:

```
Import file: biomni.tool.database
================================
Method: query_uniprot
  Description: Query the UniProt REST API using either natural language or a direct endpoint.
  Required Parameters:
    - prompt (str): Natural language query about proteins [Default: None]
  Optional Parameters:
    - endpoint (str): Full or partial UniProt API endpoint URL [Default: None]
    - max_results (int): Maximum number of results to return [Default: 5]
```

This text representation is the contract between the tool system and the LLM reasoning engine — the agent writes Python code that imports from these modules and calls these functions, and the execution layer resolves the imports accordingly.

Sources: [utils.py](/biomni/utils.py#L807-L842)

## Architectural Summary

The tool registry and discovery system is deliberately simple in its data structures (plain Python dictionaries and pandas DataFrames) while leveraging LLM intelligence at two critical points: schema generation for runtime-added tools, and prompt-based retrieval for query-time tool selection. This design keeps the registry lightweight and debuggable while offloading the semantic matching problem to the same LLM that powers the agent's reasoning — an elegant example of "use the model as the API."

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class ToolRegistry {
        +list~dict~ tools
        +int next_id
        +DataFrame document_df
        +register_tool(tool)
        +validate_tool(tool) bool
        +get_tool_by_name(name) dict
        +get_tool_by_id(tool_id) dict
        +get_id_by_name(name) int
        +get_name_by_id(tool_id) str
        +list_tools() list
        +remove_tool_by_id(tool_id) bool
        +remove_tool_by_name(name) bool
        +save_registry(filename)
        +load_registry(filename)$ ToolRegistry
    }

    class ToolRetriever {
        +prompt_based_retrieval(query, resources, llm) dict
        -_format_resources_for_prompt(resources) str
        -_parse_llm_response(response) dict
    }

    class A1 {
        +ToolRegistry tool_registry
        +ToolRetriever retriever
        +dict module2api
        +add_tool(api) dict
        +list_custom_tools() list
        +remove_custom_tool(name)
    }

    A1 --> ToolRegistry : creates when use_tool_retriever=True
    A1 --> ToolRetriever : instantiates alongside registry
    A1 --> "read_module2api()" : loads at init
    ToolRetriever --> ToolRegistry : reads document_df via A1
```

# Retrieval-Augmented Tool Selection



Biomni's tool ecosystem spans hundreds of domain-specific functions across genomics, molecular biology, immunology, and more. Supplying the LLM with every tool description on every query would exceed practical context limits and introduce noise that degrades reasoning quality. Retrieval-Augmented Tool Selection solves this by dispatching an LLM-powered selection phase *before* the reasoning loop begins, curating a query-specific subset of tools, datasets, software libraries, and know-how documents that are injected into the system prompt.

This page dissects the retrieval architecture end-to-end: the resource gathering pipeline, the LLM-based selection mechanism, response parsing, and how selected resources are materialized into the agent's working context.

## Architecture Overview

The retrieval subsystem operates as a pre-processing stage that sits between the user's query and the ReAct reasoning loop. It is controlled by a single configuration flag (`use_tool_retriever`) and executes identically for both synchronous (`go()`) and streaming (`go_stream()`) execution paths.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[User Query] --> B{use_tool_retriever?}
    B -- false --> F[Bypass: Use Full Resource Set]
    B -- true --> C[_prepare_resources_for_retrieval]

    C --> C1[Gather Tools from ToolRegistry]
    C --> C2[Gather Data Lake Items + Custom Data]
    C --> C3[Gather Software Libraries + Custom Software]
    C --> C4[Gather Know-How Summaries]

    C1 & C2 & C3 & C4 --> D[ToolRetriever.prompt_based_retrieval]
    D --> D1[Format Resources into Prompt]
    D1 --> D2[Invoke LLM for Selection]
    D2 --> D3[Parse Index-Based Response]
    D3 --> E[update_system_prompt_with_selected_resources]

    E --> E1[Resolve Module Names for Tools]
    E --> E2[Load Full Know-How Content]
    E --> E3[Generate Targeted System Prompt]
    E3 --> G[ReAct Reasoning Loop]

    F --> G
```

Sources: [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L1759-L1772), [retriever.py](biomni/model/retriever.py#L14-L132)

## The Resource Universe: Four Categories

The retriever operates over a unified dictionary keyed by four resource categories. Each category pools both built-in and user-extensible items, ensuring that custom additions participate in retrieval on equal footing with the default inventory.

| Category | Source | Description | Format |
|----------|--------|-------------|--------|
| **tools** | `ToolRegistry.tools` + `add_tool()` registrations | Callable function schemas with name, description, required_parameters | `dict` objects with `name`, `description`, `required_parameters` |
| **data_lake** | Filesystem scan of `data_lake/` + `add_data()` registrations | Dataset files with descriptions from `data_lake_dict` | `{"name": str, "description": str}` |
| **libraries** | `library_content_dict` + `add_software()` registrations | Python/R packages available in the execution environment | `{"name": str, "description": str}` |
| **know_how** | `KnowHowLoader` markdown documents | Best-practice guides, protocols, troubleshooting docs | `{"id": str, "name": str, "description": str}` |

All four categories are assembled in `_prepare_resources_for_retrieval()` [Lines 1646–1757](biomni/agent/a1.py#L1646-L1757). Custom data and software items are merged into their respective pools only if they are not already present, avoiding duplicates [Lines 1674–1688](biomni/agent/a1.py#L1674-L1688). Know-how documents, by contrast, use a two-phase strategy: *summaries* (id + name + short description) are sent to the retriever, while the *full content* is loaded only for documents that pass selection [Lines 1727–1744](biomni/agent/a1.py#L1727-L1744).

Sources: [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L1658-L1699), [loader.py](biomni/know_how/loader.py#L247-L256)

## The ToolRegistry: Index Space Foundation

The `ToolRegistry` class in [tool_registry.py](biomni/tool/tool_registry.py#L6-L89) provides the indexable backing store for all tool schemas. During initialization, it iterates over the `module2api` dictionary — a nested mapping of module names to API lists — and assigns each tool a sequential integer ID [Lines 7–18](biomni/tool/tool_registry.py#L7-L18). Every tool schema must contain at least `name`, `description`, and `required_parameters` to pass validation [Lines 32–34](biomni/tool/tool_registry.py#L32-L34).

The registry also maintains a `document_df` — a pandas DataFrame with columns `docid` and `document_content` — originally structured to support vector-based retrieval (though the current production path uses prompt-based selection exclusively) [Lines 15–18](biomni/tool/tool_registry.py#L15-L18). When custom tools are added via `A1.add_tool()`, the registry is updated in-place and the DataFrame is rebuilt to reflect the new inventory [Lines 300–312](biomni/agent/a1.py#L300-L312).

Sources: [tool_registry.py](biomni/tool/tool_registry.py#L6-L34), [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L208-L210)

## Prompt-Based Selection: ToolRetriever.prompt_based_retrieval

The core selection logic lives in `ToolRetriever.prompt_based_retrieval()` [Lines 14–132](biomni/model/retriever.py#L14-L132). Rather than using embedding similarity or BM25, Biomni delegates the selection decision entirely to an LLM call, which receives a structured prompt containing every available resource enumerated with positional indices.

### Prompt Structure

The prompt is composed of two sections concatenated together:

**Resource Catalog** — Each category is listed under a header with resources formatted as `"{index}. {name}: {description}"`. The `_format_resources_for_prompt()` method [Lines 134–152](biomni/model/retriever.py#L134-L152) handles three input polymorphisms: `dict` objects (extracting `name` and `description` keys), plain strings (used as-is), and arbitrary objects (reflecting `name` and `description` attributes).

**Response Format Instructions** — The LLM is instructed to return index lists in a strict machine-parseable format:

```
TOOLS: [0, 3, 5, 7, 9]
DATA_LAKE: [1, 2, 4]
LIBRARIES: [0, 2, 4, 5, 8]
KNOW_HOW: [0, 1]
```

The `KNOW_HOW` category is included only if know-how documents are present in the resources dictionary [Lines 48–71](biomni/model/retriever.py#L48-L71).

### Selection Guidelines

Nine explicit guidelines steer the LLM's selection behavior [Lines 77–87](biomni/model/retriever.py#L77-L87). Two are particularly aggressive in their recall bias:

- **Guideline 2**: *"ALWAYS prioritize database tools for general queries — include as many database tools as possible"*
- **Guideline 4**: *"For wet lab sequence type of queries, ALWAYS include molecular biology tools"*

This recall-oriented design philosophy means the retriever errs on the side of inclusion rather than exclusion. The system prompt preamble reinforces this: *"Be generous in your selection — include resources that might be useful for the task, even if they're not explicitly mentioned"* [Lines 35–36](biomni/model/retriever.py#L35-L36). The practical effect is that the context window receives a *curated superset* of resources, trading some context space for higher recall.

> [!TIP]
> The retriever uses the **same LLM instance** as the agent itself. In `A1.__init__()`, the agent's LLM is passed to `_prepare_resources_for_retrieval()` and forwarded to `prompt_based_retrieval()` via the `llm` parameter. If no LLM is explicitly provided, the retriever falls back to `ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4o")` [Line 93](biomni/model/retriever.py#L93). This means that in a custom LLM deployment (e.g., Ollama, local vLLM), the selection quality is directly tied to that model's instruction-following capability.

Sources: [retriever.py](biomni/model/retriever.py#L14-L132), [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L1700-L1702)

## Response Parsing: Regex-Based Index Extraction

The `_parse_llm_response()` method [Lines 154–203](biomni/model/retriever.py#L154-L203) extracts selected indices using four case-insensitive regex patterns:

| Category | Regex Pattern |
|----------|---------------|
| tools | `TOOLS:\s*\[(.*?)\]` |
| data_lake | `DATA_LAKE:\s*\[(.*?)\]` |
| libraries | `LIBRARIES:\s*\[(.*?)\]` |
| know_how | `KNOW[-_]HOW:\s*\[(.*?)\]` |

The parser tolerates both hyphenated and underscored variants of `KNOW_HOW`. It also handles two response formats: plain strings (from LangChain's `invoke()`) and Responses API-style lists of content blocks (`[{"type": "text", "text": "..."}]`) [Lines 160–170](biomni/model/retriever.py#L160-L170). All integer parsing is wrapped in `contextlib.suppress(ValueError)` to gracefully skip malformed entries, and a bounds check (`if i < len(resources.get(...))`) prevents index-out-of-range errors [Lines 108–130](biomni/model/retriever.py#L108-L130).

Sources: [retriever.py](biomni/model/retriever.py#L154-L203)

## From Indices to System Prompt: Resource Materialization

Once the retriever returns selected indices, two transformations occur before the reasoning loop begins.

### Tool Module Resolution

`update_system_prompt_with_selected_resources()` [Lines 1829–1941](biomni/agent/a1.py#L1829-L1941) resolves each selected tool's Python module name by cross-referencing against the `module2api` dictionary [Lines 1839–1848](biomni/agent/a1.py#L1839-L1848). This is critical because the system prompt instructs the LLM to import tools via `from [module_name] import [function_name]`. If a module cannot be resolved, the system defaults to `biomni.tool.scRNA_tools` as a fallback [Lines 1851–1853](biomni/agent/a1.py#L1851-L1853).

### Know-How Content Inflation

For selected know-how documents, the system loads the *full document content* (with metadata already stripped by `KnowHowLoader._strip_metadata()`) rather than the summary that was sent to the retriever [Lines 1727–1744](biomni/agent/a1.py#L1727-L1744). This two-phase approach — summaries for selection, full content for context — minimizes the token cost of the retrieval prompt while ensuring the agent receives complete protocol text when it matters.

### Custom Resource Highlighting

Custom tools, data, and software are extracted from the agent's internal `_custom_tools`, `_custom_data`, and `_custom_software` dictionaries and formatted with emoji prefixes (🔧, 📊, ⚙️) in a dedicated "PRIORITY CUSTOM RESOURCES" section of the system prompt [Lines 1157–1210](biomni/agent/a1.py#L1157-L1210). This ensures that user-registered resources receive prominent placement even when the retriever also selects them.

Sources: [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L1829-L1941), [loader.py](biomni/know_how/loader.py#L165-L224)

## Execution Integration: go() and go_stream()

Both public execution methods follow an identical retrieval pattern. In `A1.go()` [Lines 1759–1789](biomni/agent/a1.py#L1759-L1789):

```python
if self.use_tool_retriever:
    selected_resources_names = self._prepare_resources_for_retrieval(prompt)
    self.update_system_prompt_with_selected_resources(selected_resources_names)
```

The streaming variant `go_stream()` [Lines 1791–1828](biomni/agent/a1.py#L1791-L1828) mirrors this exactly. In both cases, the system prompt is overwritten *per query*, meaning that different invocations of the same agent instance can receive different resource subsets. When `use_tool_retriever` is `False`, the system prompt is generated once during `configure()` with the full resource inventory.

Sources: [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L1759-L1789), [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L1791-L1828)

## Configuration and Environment Control

The retrieval subsystem is governed by a single boolean flag, configurable at three levels of increasing precedence:

| Mechanism | Example | Precedence |
|-----------|---------|------------|
| `BiomniConfig` default | `BiomniConfig(use_tool_retriever=True)` | Lowest |
| Environment variable | `export BIOMNI_USE_TOOL_RETRIEVER=false` | Medium |
| Constructor argument | `A1(use_tool_retriever=False)` | Highest |

The default value in `BiomniConfig` is `True` [Line 40](biomni/config.py#L40), meaning retrieval is active out of the box. The environment variable override supports both string representations and is case-insensitive [Line 66](biomni/config.py#L66).

> [!TIP]
> When `use_tool_retriever=True` in **academic mode**, all know-how documents are included in the retrieval pool. In **commercial mode** (`commercial_mode=True`), documents with metadata fields containing `❌`, `Not Allowed`, or `Non-Commercial` are pre-filtered *before* retrieval occurs. This filtering happens in `_filter_know_how_for_commercial_mode()` [Lines 876–896](biomni/agent/a1.py#L876-L896), meaning the retriever never sees excluded documents.

Sources: [config.py](biomni/config.py#L40-L66), [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L876-L896)

## Diagnostic Output

When retrieval is active, the system prints a structured diagnostic block to stdout during each `go()` or `go_stream()` invocation [Lines 1703–1757](biomni/agent/a1.py#L1703-L1757):

```
============================================================
🔍 RESOURCE RETRIEVAL
============================================================
Using prompt-based retrieval with the agent's LLM

📚 Know-How Documents Retrieved:
  ✓ sgRNA Design Guide

------------------------------------------------------------
📊 RETRIEVAL SUMMARY:
  🔧 Tools: 47 selected
  📊 Data Lake: 12 selected
  ⚙️  Libraries: 8 selected
  📚 Know-How: 1 selected
============================================================
```

This output is useful for debugging retrieval quality and understanding which resources the LLM deemed relevant for a given query.

Sources: [a1.py](biomni/agent/a1.py#L1703-L1757)

## Navigating Further

- **[Tool Registry and Discovery](12-tool-registry-and-discovery)** for the underlying storage layer that provides the tool index space.
- **[Know-How Library](17-know-how-library)** for how documents are structured, loaded, and filtered before entering the retrieval pool.
- **[A1 Agent Core Class](9-a1-agent-core-class)** for the full agent lifecycle including how `use_tool_retriever` is wired through initialization and configuration.
- **[Configuration Reference](21-configuration-reference)** for all environment variables and `BiomniConfig` fields that control retrieval behavior.

# Domain Tool Implementations



This page documents the complete landscape of Biomni's domain-specific tool implementations — the executable backbone that transforms natural-language research requests into concrete computational biology operations. With over 150 callable tools spanning 18 biological domains plus cross-cutting infrastructure, the system covers the full analytical spectrum from single-cell genomics to drug safety surveillance. Each tool is a self-contained Python function bearing a structured API schema, enabling the agent to invoke them with precise parameterization during ReAct reasoning loops.
Sources: [tool/__init__.py](biomni/tool/__init__.py#L1-L2), [utils.py](biomni/utils.py#L356-L397)

## Architectural Overview

The domain tools follow a deliberately uniform architecture: every module in `biomni/tool/` exports Python functions that are decorated with `@tool` and paired with a corresponding schema definition in `biomni/tool/tool_description/`. The AST-based scanner [`get_tool_decorated_functions()`](biomni/utils.py#L356-L397) walks each module's parse tree, identifies decorated functions, imports the live module, and extracts callable objects for registration in the [`ToolRegistry`](biomni/tool/tool_registry.py#L6-L18). The registry validates that each tool carries the required keys — `name`, `description`, and `required_parameters` — before assigning a sequential integer ID and building a retrieval-ready DataFrame for the embedding-based tool selector.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Source Modules (biomni/tool/)"
        DM1[genomics.py]
        DM2[molecular_biology.py]
        DM3[pharmacology.py]
        DM4[database.py]
        DM5[biochemistry.py]
        DM6[immunology.py]
        DM7[genetics.py]
        DMN[... 11 more domains]
    end

    subgraph "Schema Definitions (biomni/tool/tool_description/)"
        SD1[genomics.py]
        SD2[molecular_biology.py]
        SD3[pharmacology.py]
        SD4[database.py]
        SDN[... paired schemas]
    end

    subgraph "Discovery & Registration"
        AST[AST Scanner<br/>get_tool_decorated_functions]
        TR[ToolRegistry<br/>validate → assign ID → index]
        DF[document_df<br/>Pandas DataFrame for retrieval]
    end

    subgraph "Execution Infrastructure"
        RE[ReAct Agent]
        REPL[Python REPL<br/>support_tools.py]
        TIMEOUT[Timeout Runner<br/>run_with_timeout]
    end

    DM1 & DM2 & DM3 & DM4 & DM5 & DM6 & DM7 & DMN --> AST
    SD1 & SD2 & SD3 & SD4 & SDN -.-> AST
    AST --> TR
    TR --> DF
    RE -->|"tool call by name"| TR
    TR -->|"execute function"| REPL
    REPL -->|"sandboxed"| TIMEOUT
```

The critical design constraint is that tools are **plain functions**, not class instances. This keeps invocation trivially serializable and sidesteps state-management complexity. The sole exceptions — `SegmentationTool` and `ImageRegistrationTool` in bioimaging, and `OpenFDAClient` in pharmacology — expose static convenience wrapper functions that internally instantiate the class, preserving the flat-function contract at the registry boundary.
Sources: [tool_registry.py](biomni/tool/tool_registry.py#L32-L34), [bioimaging.py](biomni/tool/bioimaging.py#L30-L579), [pharmacology.py](biomni/tool/pharmacology.py#L3457-L3641)

## Tool Schema Contract

Every tool, regardless of domain, conforms to a single schema contract enforced during registration. The schema is authored as a list of dictionaries in the parallel `tool_description/` modules and merged into the tool registry at startup. The three mandatory fields establish the retrieval vocabulary, while optional parameters and return type hints guide the agent's parameterization decisions.
Sources: [tool_description/genomics.py](biomni/tool/tool_description/genomics.py#L1-L50), [tool_description/database.py](biomni/tool/tool_description/database.py#L1-L50)

| Field | Type | Purpose | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `str` | Unique callable identifier, matches the Python function name | `"annotate_celltype_scRNA"` |
| `description` | `str` | Natural-language summary used for semantic retrieval | *"Annotate cell types based on gene markers and transferred labels using LLM"* |
| `required_parameters` | `list[dict]` | Each dict has `name`, `type`, `description`, `default` | `[{"name": "adata_filename", "type": "str", ...}]` |
| `optional_parameters` | `list[dict]` | Same structure; agent may omit these | `[{"name": "cluster", "default": "leiden", ...}]` |
| `id` | `int` | Auto-assigned sequential ID by ToolRegistry | Assigned at registration |

The `process_bio_retrieval_ducoment()` utility in [`utils.py`](biomni/utils.py#L400-L430) concatenates name, description, required params, and optional params into a single retrieval corpus string — this is what the embedding model sees when the retriever scores candidate tools for a given user query.
Sources: [utils.py](biomni/utils.py#L400-L430)
