# Configuration Reference



Biomni exposes a layered configuration system centered on the `BiomniConfig` dataclass. Configuration values flow downward from programmatic constructor arguments, through a global default instance, to environment variable overrides at the lowest level. This reference documents every configurable parameter, its resolution priority, and the behavioral effect each setting produces on the agent at runtime.

## Configuration Architecture

The configuration system follows a three-tier resolution chain. When any parameter is left unspecified, the system walks down this chain until it finds a concrete value:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Constructor Argument\n(e.g., A1(llm='gpt-4o'))"] -->|fallback| B["default_config Instance\n(biomni/config.py#L99)"]
    B -->|fallback| C["BiomniConfig Defaults\n(dataclass field values)"]
    C -->|overridden by| D["Environment Variables\n(__post_init__)"]
    D --> E["Final Effective Config"]

    style A fill:#4a90d9,color:#fff
    style B fill:#7b68ee,color:#fff
    style D fill:#e67e22,color:#fff
    style E fill:#2ecc71,color:#fff
```

The key insight is that **environment variables always win** over both constructor arguments and the global defaults, because `__post_init__` runs after the dataclass fields are assigned and unconditionally overwrites them if the corresponding env var is present. This design choice ensures that deployment environments (Docker, CI, HPC) can override any setting without modifying Python code.

Sources: [config.py](/biomni/config.py#L12-L99), [config.py](/biomni/config.py#L55-L81)

## The BiomniConfig Dataclass

All configuration is defined in a single `@dataclass` in `biomni/config.py`. A module-level singleton `default_config` is instantiated at import time and consumed by both the `A1` and `react` agent classes whenever their constructor arguments are `None`.

### Data and Execution Settings

| Parameter | Type | Default | Env Override | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|-------------|
| `path` | `str` | `"./data"` | `BIOMNI_PATH` or `BIOMNI_DATA_PATH` | Root directory for data lake and benchmark files. Created automatically if it doesn't exist. The agent creates subdirectories `biomni_data/data_lake/` and `biomni_data/benchmark/` beneath this path. |
| `timeout_seconds` | `int` | `600` | `BIOMNI_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | Maximum execution time for any single tool call or code block, applied via a threading-based timeout wrapper. |

The `timeout_seconds` parameter is passed through to the `_add_timeout_to_tools` method in both `A1` and `react` agents, where each tool function is wrapped with a `run_with_timeout` call from `biomni/utils.py`. This uses threading (not multiprocessing) so that global namespace variables persist between tool invocations within the same session.

Sources: [config.py](/biomni/config.py#L31-L33), [utils.py](/biomni/utils.py#L183-L188), [react.py](/biomni/agent/react.py#L90-L92)

### LLM Settings

| Parameter | Type | Default | Env Override | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|-------------|
| `llm` | `str` | `"claude-sonnet-4-5"` | `BIOMNI_LLM` or `BIOMNI_LLM_MODEL` | Model identifier string passed to `get_llm()`. The value is interpreted differently depending on the `source` parameter — see [LLM Source Resolution](#llm-source-resolution). |
| `temperature` | `float` | `0.7` | `BIOMNI_TEMPERATURE` | Sampling temperature for generation. Note that `gpt-5-*` models force this to `1.0` at the payload level because those models only accept the default value. |
| `source` | `str \| None` | `None` (auto-detect) | `BIOMNI_SOURCE` | Explicit provider override. When `None`, `get_llm()` uses a prefix-matching heuristic to determine the provider (see below). |
| `base_url` | `str \| None` | `None` | `BIOMNI_CUSTOM_BASE_URL` | Custom endpoint URL for self-hosted LLM serving (e.g., `"http://localhost:8000/v1"`). Only used when `source` is `"Custom"`. |
| `api_key` | `str \| None` | `None` | `BIOMNI_CUSTOM_API_KEY` | API key for custom model endpoints. **Not** used for provider keys (Anthropic, OpenAI, etc.) — those are read directly from provider-specific env vars like `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. |

Sources: [config.py](/biomni/config.py#L35-L50), [llm.py](/biomni/llm.py#L13-L21)

## LLM Source Resolution

The `get_llm()` function in `biomni/llm.py` supports eight distinct provider backends. The resolution logic follows a clear priority chain: explicit `source` argument → `LLM_SOURCE` env var → model-name heuristic.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    START["get_llm() called"] --> CHECK{"source arg<br/>provided?"}
    CHECK -->|Yes| USE["Use explicit source"]
    CHECK -->|No| ENV{"LLM_SOURCE<br/>env var set?"}
    ENV -->|Yes & valid| USE
    ENV -->|No| AUTO{"Auto-detect from<br/>model name prefix"}

    AUTO --> CLAUDE["claude-* → Anthropic"]
    AUTO --> GPT4["gpt-* → OpenAI"]
    AUTO --> GPT5["gpt-5-* → OpenAI\n(Responses API)"]
    AUTO --> AZURE["azure-* → AzureOpenAI"]
    AUTO --> GEMINI["gemini-* → Gemini"]
    AUTO --> GROQ["*groq* → Groq"]
    AUTO --> OLLAMA1["gpt-oss-* → Ollama"]
    AUTO --> OLLAMA2["Contains llama,\nmistral, qwen, etc.\n→ Ollama"]
    AUTO --> BEDROCK["anthropic.claude-*,\namazon.titan-*, etc.\n→ Bedrock"]
    AUTO --> CUSTOM{"base_url set?"}
    CUSTOM -->|Yes| CUST["Custom"]
    CUSTOM -->|No| ERROR["ValueError:\nUnable to determine"]

    style ERROR fill:#e74c3c,color:#fff
    style GPT5 fill:#f39c12,color:#fff
```

### Provider Reference Table

| Source | Model Prefix Pattern | Required Package | Required Env Vars | Special Behavior |
|--------|---------------------|-----------------|-------------------|-----------------|
| **Anthropic** | `claude-*` | `langchain-anthropic` | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | Falls back to reading from `~/.bash_profile`; `max_tokens=8192` |
| **OpenAI** | `gpt-*` (non-5) | `langchain-openai` | `OPENAI_API_KEY` | Standard Chat Completions API |
| **OpenAI (Responses)** | `gpt-5-*` | `langchain-openai` | `OPENAI_API_KEY` | Forces Responses API; drops `stop` and `temperature` from payload to avoid 400 errors |
| **AzureOpenAI** | `azure-*` | `langchain-openai` | `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_ENDPOINT` | Strips `azure-` prefix for deployment name; API version `2024-12-01-preview` |
| **Gemini** | `gemini-*` | `langchain-openai` | `GEMINI_API_KEY` | Routed through OpenAI-compatible endpoint at `generativelanguage.googleapis.com` |
| **Groq** | `*groq*` (case-insensitive) | `langchain-openai` | `GROQ_API_KEY` | Routed through OpenAI-compatible endpoint at `api.groq.com` |
| **Ollama** | `gpt-oss-*`, `*llama*`, `*mistral*`, `*qwen*`, etc. | `langchain-ollama` | None (local) | Also triggered by `/` in model name |
| **Bedrock** | `anthropic.claude-*`, `amazon.titan-*`, `meta.llama-*`, etc. | `langchain-aws` | AWS credentials | Defaults to `us-east-1`; region configurable via `AWS_REGION` |
| **Custom** | Any (when `base_url` set) | `langchain-openai` | None (self-hosted) | **Requires** `base_url`; `max_tokens=8192` |

The Anthropic backend includes a unique fallback mechanism: if `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is not found in the environment, it attempts to source it from `~/.bash_profile` via a subprocess call, which can be useful in HPC environments where keys are loaded at shell login.

Sources: [llm.py](/biomni/llm.py#L56-L143), [llm.py](/biomni/llm.py#L200-L276)

## Tool System Configuration

| Parameter | Type | Default | Env Override | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|-------------|
| `use_tool_retriever` | `bool` | `True` | `BIOMNI_USE_TOOL_RETRIEVER` | When enabled, the agent uses `ToolRetriever` for LLM-based prompt-driven retrieval to select a relevant subset of tools, data lake files, and library packages for each query. When disabled, the full tool catalog is injected into the system prompt. |

When `use_tool_retriever` is `True`, the `A1` agent initializes both a `ToolRegistry` (holding all registered tool metadata) and a `ToolRetriever` instance. Before each call to `go()` or `go_stream()`, the retriever calls `_prepare_resources_for_retrieval()` which formats the available resources and asks the LLM to select the most relevant subset. This reduces context window pressure and improves tool selection precision.

When disabled, all tools from every module are loaded into the system prompt at `configure()` time, which increases token usage but provides the agent with complete visibility into all available tools.

Sources: [config.py](/biomni/config.py#L40-L41), [a1.py](/biomni/agent/a1.py#L179-L181), [a1.py](/biomni/agent/a1.py#L1646-L1655)

## Licensing Mode: Commercial vs. Academic

| Parameter | Type | Default | Env Override | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|-------------|
| `commercial_mode` | `bool` | `False` | `BIOMNI_COMMERCIAL_MODE` | Controls which datasets and know-how documents are available. |

This setting triggers a fundamentally different data environment. The `A1.__init__()` method conditionally imports from either `biomni/env_desc.py` (academic) or `biomni/env_desc_cm.py` (commercial):

```python
if commercial_mode:
    from biomni.env_desc_cm import data_lake_dict, library_content_dict
else:
    from biomni.env_desc import data_lake_dict, library_content_dict
```

In **academic mode** (the default), the agent has access to the full catalog of 80+ data lake files including BindingDB drug affinities, DisGeNET gene-disease associations, MSigDB gene sets, OMIM genetic disorder data, Enamine compound libraries, EveBio screening results, miRTarBase microRNA interactions, and McPAS-TCR immune receptor data.

In **commercial mode**, 23 datasets are excluded because they carry non-commercial licenses (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, CC BY-NC 4.0) or proprietary restrictions. The filtered datasets include: all DDInter drug-drug interaction files, DisGeNET, Enamine REAL library, all EveBio tables, McPAS-TCR, miRDB, all miRTarBase files, all MSigDB collections, and OMIM. The remaining ~57 datasets with permissive or unspecified licenses remain available.

Additionally, the `_filter_know_how_for_commercial_mode()` method removes any know-how documents that have commercial-use restrictions from the `KnowHowLoader` index at startup.

Sources: [config.py](/biomni/config.py#L43-L44), [a1.py](/biomni/agent/a1.py#L109-L116), [env_desc_cm.py](/biomni/env_desc_cm.py#L1-L80), [a1.py](/biomni/agent/a1.py#L876-L882)

## Agent-Level Configuration

Beyond `BiomniConfig`, both the `A1` and `react` agent classes expose additional configuration points through their constructors and methods.

### A1 Constructor Parameters

The `A1` class accepts every `BiomniConfig` field as an optional constructor argument, with one addition:

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `expected_data_lake_files` | `list \| None` | `None` (all files) | When explicitly provided (non-None), the agent skips automatic S3 data lake download. Set to an empty list `[]` to disable download entirely. |

The constructor falls back to `default_config` for any unspecified parameter, then prints a formatted configuration summary to stdout showing both the default config values and any agent-level overrides.

Sources: [a1.py](/biomni/agent/a1.py#L57-L68), [a1.py](/biomni/agent/a1.py#L121-L181)

### A1.configure() Parameters

The `configure()` method, called automatically at the end of `__init__`, accepts runtime behavioral flags:

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `self_critic` | `bool` | `False` | Enables self-critic mode where the agent reviews and potentially revises its own output before finalizing. |
| `test_time_scale_round` | `int` | `0` | Number of additional reasoning rounds for test-time compute scaling. Higher values increase reasoning depth at the cost of latency and token usage. |

These parameters modify the agent's LangGraph workflow structure — specifically, they change how the system prompt is generated and how many reasoning iterations the graph allows before terminating.

Sources: [a1.py](/biomni/agent/a1.py#L1289-L1297)

### react Constructor Parameters

The lightweight `react` agent accepts a subset of configuration:

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `path` | `str \| None` | From `default_config` | Data directory path |
| `llm` | `str \| None` | From `default_config` | LLM model name |
| `use_tool_retriever` | `bool \| None` | From `default_config` | Tool retrieval toggle |
| `timeout_seconds` | `int \| None` | From `default_config` | Execution timeout |

The `react` agent does **not** support `source`, `base_url`, `api_key`, or `commercial_mode` — it always uses the global default config for LLM resolution and always operates in academic mode.

Sources: [react.py](/biomni/agent/react.py#L39-L53)

## Execution Parameters

Several configuration values are hardcoded within the agent internals rather than exposed through `BiomniConfig`:

| Parameter | Value | Location | Description |
|-----------|-------|----------|-------------|
| `recursion_limit` | `500` | `A1.go()`, `A1.go_stream()`, `launch_gradio_demo()` | Maximum number of LangGraph node traversals per agent invocation. Acts as a safety bound against infinite loops in the reasoning graph. |
| `thread_id` | `42` | `A1.go()`, `launch_gradio_demo()` | LangGraph checkpointing thread identifier. Change this to isolate conversation states. |
| `stop_sequences` | `["</execute>", "</solution>"]` | `A1.__init__()` | Custom stop tokens that tell the LLM when to end its code-generation or solution-generation phase. |
| `max_tokens` | `8192` | `get_llm()` for Anthropic, Custom | Maximum output token count for Anthropic and custom-served models. |

Sources: [a1.py](/biomni/agent/a1.py#L1766-L1767), [a1.py](/biomni/agent/a1.py#L1791-L1792), [llm.py](/biomni/llm.py#L139-L142), [llm.py](/biomni/llm.py#L257-L264)

## Gradio Interface Configuration

The `launch_gradio_demo()` method exposes its own set of launch parameters independent of `BiomniConfig`:

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `thread_id` | `int` | `42` | LangGraph checkpoint thread for the Gradio session. |
| `share` | `bool` | `False` | Create a public Gradio shareable link (useful for remote demos). |
| `server_name` | `str` | `"0.0.0.0"` | Network interface to bind. Use `"127.0.0.1"` for local-only access. |
| `require_verification` | `bool` | `False` | When enabled, presents an access code gate before the chat interface. Default access code is `"Biomni2025"`. |

Sources: [a1.py](/biomni/agent/a1.py#L2627-L2636)

## Third-Party Integrations

| Parameter | Type | Default | Env Override | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|-------------|
| `protocols_io_access_token` | `str \| None` | `None` | `PROTOCOLS_IO_ACCESS_TOKEN` or `BIOMNI_PROTOCOLS_IO_ACCESS_TOKEN` | Authentication token for the Protocols.io API, used for retrieving experimental protocols. The env var resolution prefers the specific `PROTOCOLS_IO_ACCESS_TOKEN` over the `BIOMNI_`-prefixed alias. |

Sources: [config.py](/biomni/config.py#L53-L54), [config.py](/biomni/config.py#L78-L81)

## Complete Environment Variable Reference

The following table consolidates every environment variable the configuration system recognizes, including backward-compatible aliases:

| Environment Variable | Primary / Alias | Maps To | Accepted Values |
|---------------------|-----------------|---------|-----------------|
| `BIOMNI_PATH` | Primary | `BiomniConfig.path` | Directory path string |
| `BIOMNI_DATA_PATH` | Alias | `BiomniConfig.path` | Directory path string |
| `BIOMNI_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | Primary | `BiomniConfig.timeout_seconds` | Integer string |
| `BIOMNI_LLM` | Primary | `BiomniConfig.llm` | Model identifier string |
| `BIOMNI_LLM_MODEL` | Alias | `BiomniConfig.llm` | Model identifier string |
| `BIOMNI_TEMPERATURE` | Primary | `BiomniConfig.temperature` | Float string |
| `BIOMNI_USE_TOOL_RETRIEVER` | Primary | `BiomniConfig.use_tool_retriever` | `"true"` / `"false"` (case-insensitive) |
| `BIOMNI_COMMERCIAL_MODE` | Primary | `BiomniConfig.commercial_mode` | `"true"` / `"false"` (case-insensitive) |
| `BIOMNI_CUSTOM_BASE_URL` | Primary | `BiomniConfig.base_url` | URL string |
| `BIOMNI_CUSTOM_API_KEY` | Primary | `BiomniConfig.api_key` | API key string |
| `BIOMNI_SOURCE` | Primary | `BiomniConfig.source` | `OpenAI`, `AzureOpenAI`, `Anthropic`, `Ollama`, `Gemini`, `Bedrock`, `Groq`, `Custom` |
| `LLM_SOURCE` | Provider-level | `get_llm()` source resolution | Same valid sources as above |
| `PROTOCOLS_IO_ACCESS_TOKEN` | Primary | `BiomniConfig.protocols_io_access_token` | Token string |
| `BIOMNI_PROTOCOLS_IO_ACCESS_TOKEN` | Alias | `BiomniConfig.protocols_io_access_token` | Token string |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | Provider | Anthropic backend | Anthropic API key |
| `OPENAI_API_KEY` | Provider | OpenAI, AzureOpenAI, Gemini, Groq backends | Provider API key |
| `OPENAI_ENDPOINT` | Provider | AzureOpenAI backend | Azure endpoint URL |
| `GEMINI_API_KEY` | Provider | Gemini backend | Google API key |
| `GROQ_API_KEY` | Provider | Groq backend | Groq API key |
| `AWS_REGION` | Provider | Bedrock backend | AWS region (default: `us-east-1`) |

> [!TIP]
> **Priority trap**: Because `__post_init__` runs after dataclass field assignment, an environment variable will **always** override a constructor argument. If you need programmatic control in an environment that has `BIOMNI_LLM` set, you must either unset the env var before constructing the agent or set it explicitly after construction via `agent.llm = get_llm("your-model")`.

Sources: [config.py](/biomni/config.py#L55-L81), [llm.py](/biomni/llm.py#L67-L77)

## Configuration Examples

### Minimal: Use All Defaults

```python
from biomni.agent import A1

agent = A1()
# Uses: claude-sonnet-4-5, temperature=0.7, ./data, academic mode, tool retriever on
```

### Override via Constructor

```python
agent = A1(
    llm="gpt-4o",
    temperature=0.3,
    timeout_seconds=1200,
    commercial_mode=True,
)
```

### Override via Environment Variables

```bash
export BIOMNI_LLM="gpt-4o"
export BIOMNI_TEMPERATURE="0.3"
export BIOMNI_COMMERCIAL_MODE="true"
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="sk-ant-..."  # Still needed for Anthropic tools' internal LLM
python -c "from biomni.agent import A1; a = A1()"
```

### Custom Model Serving (e.g., SGLang)

```python
agent = A1(
    llm="meta-llama/Llama-3-70B-Instruct",
    source="Custom",
    base_url="http://localhost:8000/v1",
    api_key="not-needed",
)
```

### Configure Self-Critic Mode

```python
agent = A1(llm="claude-sonnet-4-5")
agent.configure(self_critic=True, test_time_scale_round=2)
```

## Next Steps

- For a walkthrough of setting up API keys for each provider, see [API Key Configuration](3-api-key-configuration).
- To understand how configuration flows into the agent's reasoning workflow, see [A1 Agent Core Class](9-a1-agent-core-class).
- For the differences between commercial and academic datasets in detail, see [Commercial vs Academic Mode](20-commercial-vs-academic-mode).
- For environment setup and dependency installation, see [Environment Setup and Dependencies](22-environment-setup-and-dependencies).

# Environment Setup and Dependencies



Biomni's dependency landscape is divided into two cleanly separated layers: a **Python package layer** managed through `pyproject.toml` and `environment.yml`, and a **bioinformatics tool layer** managed through conda-forge/bioconda channels plus a JSON-driven CLI tool installer. The project requires Python ≥ 3.11 and is officially tested only on Ubuntu 22.04 (64-bit). This page walks you through each installation tier, the tradeoffs between them, and how to incrementally update an existing environment.

Sources: [pyproject.toml](pyproject.toml#L1-L16), [README.md](biomni_env/README.md#L1-L30)

## Architecture of the Environment Tiers

Biomni provides four distinct environment profiles, each occupying a different point on the spectrum of completeness versus setup time and disk usage. The diagram below illustrates the layered relationship between these tiers and how they compose.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Layer 1: Python Core"
        A["environment.yml<br/>~5 min · ~3 GB<br/>Agent runtime + LLM integrations"]
    end
    subgraph "Layer 2: Bioinformatics Libraries"
        B["bio_env.yml<br/>(merged into A via setup.sh)"]
        C["r_packages.yml<br/>R 4.4+ + Bioconductor"]
        D["install_r_packages.R<br/>DESeq2, WGCNA, clusterProfiler…"]
    end
    subgraph "Layer 3: CLI Binaries"
        E["install_cli_tools.sh<br/>PLINK2, IQ-TREE, GCTA, HOMER…"]
    end
    subgraph "Alternative Profiles"
        F["fixed_env.yml<br/>~13 GB · No R/CLI<br/>Pinned versions"]
        G["bio_env_py310.yml<br/>cnvkit + Python 3.10"]
    end

    A --> B
    A --> C
    C --> D
    B --> E

    A -.->|"subset of A+B"| F
    A -.->|"separate env"| G
```

Sources: [setup.sh](biomni_env/setup.sh#L152-L191), [README.md](biomni_env/README.md#L12-L44)

## Environment Profile Comparison

| Profile | Conda File | Env Name | Disk Space | Setup Time | Includes | Best For |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Basic Agent** | `environment.yml` | `biomni_e1` | ~3 GB | ~5 min | LangChain, MCP, basic Python libs | Quick start, custom tool integration, API-only usage |
| **Full E1** | `setup.sh` (orchestrator) | `biomni_e1` | ~30 GB | >10 hours | Everything below | Benchmark evaluation, full tool coverage |
| **Reduced/Fixed** | `fixed_env.yml` | `biomni_e1` | ~13 GB | ~30 min | Pinned conda + bioinformatics (no R, no CLI) | Stable development, reproducible builds |
| **Python 3.10** | `bio_env_py310.yml` | `bio_env_py310` | ~2 GB | ~10 min | cnvkit + samtools + bedtools | Copy number analysis only |

Sources: [README.md](biomni_env/README.md#L12-L46), [pyproject.toml](pyproject.toml#L6-L16), [fixed_env.yml](biomni_env/fixed_env.yml#L1-L6), [bio_env_py310.yml](biomni_env/bio_env_py310.yml#L1-L8)

## Tier 1: Basic Agent Environment

The `environment.yml` file defines the minimal viable environment for running the Biomni agent. It targets Python 3.11 and installs all core LLM integration packages via pip within a conda wrapper. The three channels—`conda-forge`, `defaults`, and `bioconda`—are declared here even though the basic tier doesn't use bioconda packages directly; this ensures that subsequent `conda env update` operations from higher-tier files resolve correctly against the same channel priority.

The pip dependency set in `environment.yml` includes the LangChain ecosystem (`langchain`, `langgraph==0.3.18`, `langchain-openai`, `langchain-anthropic`, `langchain-ollama`, `langchain-community`), the MCP protocol library (`mcp`), the `tooluniverse` package for tool discovery, and scientific computing staples (`numpy==2.1`, `pandas`, `scipy`, `scikit-learn`, `statsmodels`). Gradio is included here for web interface support, and `transformers` + `sentencepiece` provide local model inference capabilities.

To create this environment:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/snap-stanford/Biomni.git
cd Biomni/biomni_env
conda env create -f environment.yml
conda activate biomni_e1
```

Sources: [environment.yml](biomni_env/environment.yml#L1-L39), [README.md](biomni_env/README.md#L1-L16)

## Tier 2: Full E1 Environment (setup.sh)

The full environment is the one used for Biomni-Eval1 benchmark evaluation. It is built by the orchestrator script `setup.sh`, which executes six sequential steps, each corresponding to a distinct installation layer. This script includes error handling with interactive fallback prompts (or non-interactive continuation via the `NON_INTERACTIVE` environment variable) and supports both conda and micromamba as the package manager backend.

The six-step installation flow proceeds as follows:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    S1["Step 1: conda env create<br/>environment.yml<br/>(base Python + LLM libs)"]
    S2["Step 2: conda activate biomni_e1"]
    S3["Step 3: conda env update<br/>bio_env.yml<br/>(BLAST, samtools, scanpy, rdkit…)"]
    S4["Step 4: conda env update<br/>r_packages.yml<br/>(R 4.4+ + r-essentials)"]
    S5["Step 5: Rscript install_r_packages.R<br/>(DESeq2, WGCNA, clusterProfiler…)"]
    S6["Step 6: bash install_cli_tools.sh<br/>(PLINK2, IQ-TREE, GCTA, HOMER…)"]

    S1 -->|"non-interactive:<br/>NON_INTERACTIVE=1"| S2
    S2 --> S3
    S3 --> S4
    S4 --> S5
    S5 --> S6
```

Sources: [setup.sh](biomni_env/setup.sh#L1-L34), [setup.sh](biomni_env/setup.sh#L152-L191)

### Bioinformatics Libraries (bio_env.yml)

The `bio_env.yml` file extends the base environment with conda-forge/bioconda system-level tools and a large set of Python bioinformatics packages. On the conda side, it installs sequence alignment tools (`blast`, `bowtie2`, `bwa`), variant calling infrastructure (`samtools`, `bedtools`), quality control (`fastqc`, `trimmomatic`), multiple sequence alignment (`mafft`), and CRISPR screening analysis (`mageck`). The pip section is substantially larger, covering single-cell analysis (`scanpy`, `scvelo`, `scvi-tools`, `harmony-pytorch`, `scrublet`), structural biology (`rdkit`, `openmm`, `biotite`), genomic data formats (`pysam`, `pyfaidx`, `pyranges`, `pybedtools`, `cooler`, `cyvcf2`), systems biology (`cobra` for metabolic models, `pyscenic` for gene regulatory networks), drug discovery (`pytdc==0.4.0`), literature mining (`pymed`, `scholarly`, `arxiv`), and imaging (`cellpose`, `scikit-image`). Notably, `faiss-cpu` provides the vector similarity search backend used by the retrieval-augmented tool selection system.

Sources: [bio_env.yml](biomni_env/bio_env.yml#L1-L71)

### R Packages

R support is split across two stages. First, `r_packages.yml` installs `r-essentials` and `r-base>=4.4` via conda. Then `install_r_packages.R` uses R's native package manager and BiocManager to install domain-specific packages: CRAN packages including `ggplot2`, `lme4`, `harmony`, and the Tidyverse suite, plus Bioconductor packages `DESeq2`, `dada2`, `xcms`, `flowCore`, `edgeR`, and `limma`. The script also installs `WGCNA` with its complex dependency chain (including Bioconductor packages `impute`, `preprocessCore`, `GO.db`, `AnnotationDbi`) and `clusterProfiler` for functional enrichment analysis. Each package is wrapped in an `install_if_missing` guard to support idempotent re-runs.

Sources: [r_packages.yml](biomni_env/r_packages.yml#L1-L8), [install_r_packages.R](biomni_env/install_r_packages.R#L1-L133)

### CLI Tools (install_cli_tools.sh)

The CLI tool installer is the most architecturally sophisticated component of the environment system. Rather than hardcoding tool installations, it reads from a declarative JSON configuration file (`cli_tools_config.json`) that specifies each tool's name, description, platform-specific download URLs (Linux, macOS Intel, macOS ARM64), binary path within the archive, and version command. The installer supports three archive formats (`.zip`, `.tar.gz`, and raw binary) and includes special-case handlers for tools that require compilation (`FastTree` compiled with GCC, `BWA` compiled via `make`) or custom installation workflows (`HOMER` installed via its Perl-based `configureHomer.pl` script).

All tools are installed to a configurable directory (default: `./biomni_tools`) and symlinked into a `bin/` subdirectory that is added to `PATH`. The script generates helper files (`setup_path.sh`, `test_tools.sh`, `fix_path.sh`) and can optionally modify the user's shell profile for persistent PATH configuration. It also handles shell command hash table invalidation (`hash -r` / `rehash`) to prevent stale path caching issues.

The seven tools currently configured in `cli_tools_config.json`:

| Tool | Domain | Installation Method |
|---|---|---|
| **PLINK 2.0** | GWAS / whole-genome association | Pre-built binary (per-platform) |
| **IQ-TREE 2.2.2.7** | Phylogenetic ML inference | Pre-built binary (per-platform) |
| **GCTA 1.94.x** | Genome-wide complex trait analysis | Pre-built binary (per-platform) |
| **BWA** | Short-read alignment | Git clone + `make` compilation |
| **FastTree** | Approximate-ML phylogenetic trees | Source compilation with GCC |
| **MUSCLE 5.3** | Multiple sequence alignment | Raw binary download |
| **HOMER** | Motif discovery / ChIP-seq analysis | Perl installer script |

To install CLI tools standalone (without the full setup.sh pipeline), set `BIOMNI_AUTO_INSTALL=1` for non-interactive mode or run the script directly for an interactive menu:

```bash
cd biomni_env
export BIOMNI_TOOLS_DIR="$HOME/biomni_tools"
export BIOMNI_AUTO_INSTALL=1
bash install_cli_tools.sh
source ~/biomni_tools/setup_path.sh
```

> [!TIP]
> If you encounter "No such file or directory" errors after installation, your shell is likely caching stale binary paths. Run `hash -r` (bash) or `rehash` (zsh), or use the generated fix script: `source $TOOLS_DIR/fix_path.sh`. This is the single most common post-installation issue.

Sources: [cli_tools_config.json](biomni_env/cli_tools_config.json#L1-L94), [install_cli_tools.sh](biomni_env/install_cli_tools.sh#L66-L103), [install_cli_tools.sh](biomni_env/install_cli_tools.sh#L408-L453)

## Tier 3: Reduced/Fixed Environment

The `fixed_env.yml` file provides a middle ground between the basic agent and the full E1 environment. It is a single monolithic conda environment file with **pinned versions** for every dependency (743 lines total), combining the Python packages from `environment.yml` and the bioinformatics conda packages from `bio_env.yml` into one reproducible specification. It deliberately excludes R packages and CLI tools, reducing the disk footprint to approximately 13 GB. Some packages from `bio_env.yml` that had dependency issues are commented out (e.g., `mageck`, `plannotate`), reflecting the maintainers' effort to produce a conflict-free environment.

This is the recommended profile for **development and testing** where you need bioinformatics library support but don't want to invest in the full multi-hour setup process.

```bash
conda env create -f fixed_env.yml
conda activate biomni_e1
```

Sources: [fixed_env.yml](biomni_env/fixed_env.yml#L1-L10), [fixed_env.yml](biomni_env/fixed_env.yml#L142-L186), [README.md](biomni_env/README.md#L32-L38)

## Incremental Updates (new_software_v008.sh)

When new packages are introduced in a release, the `new_software_v008.sh` script provides an incremental update path for existing environments. The current version installs or updates packages including `transformers`, `sentencepiece`, `langchain-google-genai`, `langchain_ollama`, `mcp`, `lazyslide`, `uv`, `pybiomart`, `fair-esm` (protein language models), `nnunet`/`nibabel`/`nilearn` (medical imaging), `pylabrobot` (lab automation), and `weasyprint`. Some packages require non-standard installation methods: `transcriptformer` is installed via `uv pip install` due to build constraints, `popV` is installed from a specific GitHub PR branch, and `arc-state` is installed as a `uv tool`. The script also initializes git-lfs support for large file handling.

```bash
conda activate biomni_e1
cd biomni_env
bash new_software_v008.sh
```

Sources: [new_software_v008.sh](biomni_env/new_software_v008.sh#L1-L19)

## Python Package Installation via pip

For developers who want to install the Biomni Python package itself (rather than just its dependencies), `pyproject.toml` defines a minimal set of three runtime dependencies: `pydantic`, `langchain`, and `python-dotenv`. The project uses setuptools with dynamic versioning sourced from `biomni/version.py`, and includes an optional `gradio` extra for web interface support. The `MANIFEST.in` file ensures that tool schema databases (`*.pkl` files under `biomni/tool/schema_db/`) and all environment configuration files are included in distribution packages.

```bash
pip install -e .                   # Editable install with core deps
pip install -e ".[gradio]"         # With Gradio web interface
```

Sources: [pyproject.toml](pyproject.toml#L1-L32), [MANIFEST.in](MANIFEST.in#L1-L28)

## LLM Provider Extensions

The base environment includes LangChain integrations for three providers: OpenAI (`langchain-openai`), Anthropic (`langchain-anthropic`), and Ollama (`langchain-ollama`) for local model serving. Additional providers require manual installation:

```bash
pip install langchain-google-genai   # Google Gemini
pip install langchain-aws            # Amazon Bedrock
```

Note that `langchain_aws` is documented as having known dependency conflicts with the main environment. If Bedrock support is required, you should install it in a separate virtual environment or with careful version pinning. See [known_conflicts.md](docs/known_conflicts.md) for the full conflict registry.

Sources: [README.md](biomni_env/README.md#L58-L74), [known_conflicts.md](docs/known_conflicts.md#L1-L35)

## Known Package Conflicts

Several packages are deliberately excluded from the default environment due to irreconcilable dependency conflicts. These are documented in `docs/known_conflicts.md` and summarized here:

| Package | Conflict Reason | Workaround |
|---|---|---|
| `hyperimpute` | Dependency conflicts with main environment | Install in separate env |
| `langchain_aws` | Conflicts with other langchain packages; requires uncommenting Bedrock code | Manual install + code changes |
| `cnvkit` | Requires Python 3.10; conflicts with Python 3.11 packages | Use `bio_env_py310.yml` |
| `panhumanpy` | Requires TensorFlow 2.17 + scikit-learn 1.6.0 (specific versions) | Install in dedicated env |

The cnvkit workaround is integrated into the environment system: running `conda env create -f bio_env_py310.yml` creates a `bio_env_py310` environment that can be invoked via `conda run -n bio_env_py310 <command>` for copy number analysis tasks without contaminating the main environment.

Sources: [known_conflicts.md](docs/known_conflicts.md#L1-L35), [bio_env_py310.yml](biomni_env/bio_env_py310.yml#L13-L20)

## Configuration via Environment Variables

Once the environment is activated, runtime behavior can be tuned through environment variables that are read by the `BiomniConfig` dataclass. These are orthogonal to the dependency installation process but are worth noting here because some (like `BIOMNI_PATH`) affect which tools and data the agent can access:

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `BIOMNI_PATH` / `BIOMNI_DATA_PATH` | `./data` | Data directory for tool outputs |
| `BIOMNI_LLM` / `BIOMNI_LLM_MODEL` | `claude-sonnet-4-5` | LLM model selection |
| `BIOMNI_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | `600` | Per-tool execution timeout |
| `BIOMNI_USE_TOOL_RETRIEVER` | `true` | Enable retrieval-augmented tool selection |
| `BIOMNI_COMMERCIAL_MODE` | `false` | Exclude non-commercial datasets |
| `BIOMNI_CUSTOM_BASE_URL` | `None` | Custom LLM endpoint URL |
| `BIOMNI_SOURCE` | `None` | Auto-detected LLM source override |
| `PROTOCOLS_IO_ACCESS_TOKEN` | `None` | Protocols.io API access token |

Sources: [config.py](biomni/config.py#L12-L81)

## Troubleshooting Common Setup Issues

| Symptom | Cause | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| `conda env create` fails on channel resolution | Network issues or channel priority | Ensure `conda-forge` is highest priority; try `conda env create -f environment.yml --dry-run` first |
| R packages fail to compile | Missing system libraries (e.g., `libcurl`, `libxml2`) | Install via `conda install -c conda-forge r-base r-essentials` before running `install_r_packages.R` |
| CLI tools report "command not found" | PATH not updated or shell hash cache | Run `source $TOOLS_DIR/setup_path.sh && hash -r` |
| `langgraph` version mismatch | `langgraph==0.3.18` is pinned for compatibility | Do not upgrade; check [Configuration Reference](21-configuration-reference) for version requirements |
| `setup.sh` takes >10 hours | This is expected for the full E1 environment | Use `fixed_env.yml` for a faster alternative (~30 min) |
| Python 3.10 tool fails in 3.11 env | cnvkit requires Python 3.10 | Use `conda run -n bio_env_py310 <command>` to invoke tools from the separate environment |

---

For next steps in your setup journey, configure your LLM provider API keys in [API Key Configuration](3-api-key-configuration), then explore the agent's runtime behavior in [Architecture Overview](8-architecture-overview). If you plan to extend the tool system with your own bioinformatics packages, refer to [Custom Tools and Data](18-custom-tools-and-data) and the [Tool Registry and Discovery](12-tool-registry-and-discovery) documentation.
